29-09-02-000-801Air Charging Valve Manifold Assembly - Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-801

Task Description

2. Air Charging Valve Manifold Assembly - Removal (Figure 201)

A. General

(1) This task has instructions for the removal of the air charging valve and it's manifold assembly. It is not necessary to remove the manifold assembly to remove the air charging valve.

B. References

Reference Title 20-10-44-000-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Removal (P/B 401) 29-00-00-800-801 Hydraulic Power System - Deactivation (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201)

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-14686 Fittings - Hydraulic, Caps/Plugs (ref. AMM 20-10-XX)

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

E. Prepare for Removal

SUBTASK 29-09-02-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. WARNING REMOVE THE PRESSURE FROM THE PNEUMATIC DUCTS BEFORE YOU REMOVE A PNEUMATIC SYSTEM COMPONENT . HOT HIGH PRESSURE AIR CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Do this task: Hydraulic Power System - Deactivation, TASK 29-00-00-800-801. SUBTASK 29-09-02-010-001 (3) Get access to the manifold assembly [1] in the right main landing gear wheel well. 29-09-02 SUBTASK 29-09-02-210-001 (4) Do not touch the manifold assembly [1] until it has cooled. NOTE: If the pneumatic system was in operation previously, allow time for the manifold assembly to become cool before you touch it. F. Manifold Assembly Removal SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-004 (1) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are depressurized before you remove the manifold assembly [1] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802). SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-001 (2) Loosen the tube assembly nuts [5] to disconnect the tube assemblies from the elbow [12] and union [6] on the manifold assembly [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-002 (3) Remove the bolts [2] and washers [3] that attach the manifold assembly [1] to the bracket. SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-007 (4) Remove the manifold assembly [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-008 (5) Remove the elbow [12] from the union [6]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-003 (6) Remove the unions [6] from the manifold assembly [1]. (a) Remove and discard the packings [7] (o-rings) from the unions [6]. (b) Set aside unions [6] for later installation. SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-001 (7) Install cap/plug, STD-14686, to the tube assembly nuts [5] and ports of manifold assembly [1].

G. Air Charging Valve Removal

SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-005 (1) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are depressurized before you remove the charging valve [4] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802). SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-004 (2) Remove the lockwire from the charging valve [4] and manifold assembly [1] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-005 (3) Remove the charging valve [4] from the manifold assembly [1]. (a) Remove and discard the packing [11] (o-ring) from the charging valve [4].

29-09-02-400-801Air Charging Valve Manifold Assembly - Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-801

Task Description

3. Air Charging Valve Manifold Assembly - Installation (Figure 201)

A. References

Reference Title 20-10-44-400-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation (P/B 401) 29-00-00-800-802 Hydraulic Power System - Activation (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-801 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201)

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-14686 Fittings - Hydraulic, Caps/Plugs (ref. AMM 20-10-XX)

C. Consumable Materials

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

E. Manifold Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-006 (1) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the tube assembly nuts [5] and ports of manifold assembly [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-640-001 (2) Lightly lubricate the new packings [7] (O-rings) with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-008 (3) Install the new packings [7] (O-rings) onto the unions [6]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-002 (4) Install the unions [6] into the ports of manifold assembly [1] and tighten to 150 in-lb (17 N·m) - 300 in-lb (34 N·m). SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-010 (5) Install the elbow [12] onto the union [6] and tighten to 133 in-lb (15 N·m) - 147 in-lb (17 N·m). SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-003 (6) Install the manifold assembly [1] to the bracket with the bolts [2], washers [3], and tighten. SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-004 (7) Connect the tube assembly nuts [5] to the elbow [12], unions [6], and tighten to 133 in-lb (15 N·m) - 147 in-lb (17 N·m). 29-09-02 F. Air Charging Valve Installation SUBTASK 29-09-02-640-002 (1) Lightly lubricate the new packing [11] (O-ring) with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-009 (2) Install the packing [11] (O-ring) onto the charging valve [4]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-005 NOTE: Clean top surface of BOSS and insure that it is free from nicks and scratches before installing charging valve. (3) Insert the charging valve [4] into the port of the manifold assembly [1]. (a) Tighten the charging valve [4] to 100 in-lb (11 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12 N·m). SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-006 (4) Install a MS20995C47 lockwire, G50356, to the air charging valve [4] and manifold assembly [1] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-007 (5) Make sure that the dust cap [9] is installed to extreme finger tightness and the swivel nut [8] is turned to the fully closed position on the charging valve [4]. (a) Tighten the swivel nut [8] to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m).

G. Post-Installation Leakage Check

SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-006 (1) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-09-02-790-001 (2) Use a solution of soap and water to check that no air leaks at the all connections on the manifold assembly [1] and charging valve [4]. SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-008 (3) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-09-02-840-001 (1) Do this task: Hydraulic Power System - Activation, TASK 29-00-00-800-802.

(3) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806. SUBTASK 29-09-03-860-003 (4) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 29-09-03-010-001 (5) Get access to the air pressure gauge [1] in the right main landing gear wheel well.

E. Air Pressure Gauge Removal

SUBTASK 29-09-03-860-004 (1) Make sure the hydraulic reservoirs have been depressurized before you remove the air pressure gauge [1] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802). (a) Remove the dust cap on the air charging valve then slowly unscrew the swivel nut to release any residual air pressure. (b) Reinstall dust cap and tighten swivel nut. (c) Make sure the air pressure gauge [1] reads 0 psi. SUBTASK 29-09-03-020-001 (2) Loosen the swivel nut to disconnect the elbow from the air pressure gauge [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-03-020-002 (3) Remove the nut [2] and washer [3] to remove the air pressure gauge [1] from the bracket. SUBTASK 29-09-03-420-001 (4) Install plug/cap to the tube end and air pressure gauge port.

29-09-03-400-801Air Pressure Gauge - Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-801

Task Description

3. Air Pressure Gauge - Installation (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 29-09-00-860-801 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201)

B. Expendables/Parts

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Air Pressure Gauge Installation

SUBTASK 29-09-03-020-003 (1) Remove the plug/cap from the tube end and air pressure gauge [1] port. SUBTASK 29-09-03-420-002 (2) Install the air pressure gauge [1] to the bracket with the nut [2] and washer [3], and tighten. NOTE: The 'green' band on the gauge scale should point to the 12 o'clock position (vertical) for ease of readout. SUBTASK 29-09-03-420-003 (3) Connect the elbow to the air pressure gauge [1] and tighten the swivel nut.

E. Post-Installation Leakage Check

SUBTASK 29-09-03-860-005 (1) Pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold duct. (a) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801. (b) Make sure that the indicated pressure is within 10 psi of the duct pressure indication. NOTE: The permitted operating range of pressure is between 12–65 psi depending on the pneumatic source available and aircraft operation. 29-09-03 SUBTASK 29-09-03-790-001 (2) Use a solution of soap and water to check that there are no air leaks at the swivel nut connection. SUBTASK 29-09-03-860-006 (3) Release the pressure from the pneumatic crossover manifold duct. (a) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802.

29-09-04-000-801Cross Fitting Assembly - Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-801

Task Description

2. Cross Fitting Assembly - Removal (Figure 201)

A. General

(1) This task has instructions for the removal of the cross fitting assembly.

B. References

Reference Title 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 29-21-00-000-802 Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201) 36-00-00-860-806 Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Prepare for Removal

SUBTASK 29-09-04-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-001 (2) Do these tasks to remove hydraulic power if supplied to the airplane: (a) For the main hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805 (b) For the standby hydraulic system, do this task: Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802 29-09-04 SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-002 WARNING YOU MUST REMOVE THE PRESSURE FROM THE PNEUMATIC DUCTS BEFORE YOU REMOVE A PNEUMATIC SYSTEM COMPONENT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE THE PRESSURE FROM THE PNEUMATIC DUCTS, HOT HIGH PRESSURE AIR CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806. SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-003 (4) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 29-09-04-010-001 (5) Get access to the cross fitting assembly in the right main landing gear wheel well. SUBTASK 29-09-04-210-001 (6) Do not touch the cross fitting assembly until it has cooled. NOTE: If the pneumatic system was in operation previously, allow time for the cross fitting assembly to become cool before you touch it.

E. Cross Fitting Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-004 (1) Make sure the hydraulic reservoirs have been depressurized before you remove the cross fitting assembly (TASK 29-09-00-860-802). (a) Remove the dust cap on the air charging valve then slowly unscrew the swivel nut to release any residual air pressure. (b) Reinstall dust cap and tighten swivel nut. (c) Make sure the air pressure gauge reads 0 psi. SUBTASK 29-09-04-020-001 (2) Loosen the swivel nut to disconnect the elbow [7] from the restrictor [6] on the cross fitting [1] assemlby. SUBTASK 29-09-04-020-005 (3) Loosen the swivel nut to disconnect the elbow [4] from the check valve [3] on the cross fitting [1] assembly. SUBTASK 29-09-04-020-002 (4) Loosen the swivel nut [9] and coupling nut [8] to disconnect the pressure relief valve and adjacent hydraulic reservoir tubing from the cross fitting [1] assembly. SUBTASK 29-09-04-020-003 (5) Remove the cross fitting [1] assembly. SUBTASK 29-09-04-420-001 (6) Install plugs/caps to the tube ends and cross fitting assembly ports.

29-09-04-400-801Cross Fitting Assembly - Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-801

Task Description

3. Cross Fitting Assembly - Installation (Figure 201)

A. References

Reference Title 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

C. Cross Fitting Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 29-09-04-020-004 (1) Remove the plugs/caps from the tube ends and cross fitting assembly ports. SUBTASK 29-09-04-420-002 (2) Put the cross fitting [1] assembly between the pressure relief valve and adjacent hydraulic reservoir tubing and loosely connect the swivel nut [9] and coupling nut [8]. SUBTASK 29-09-04-420-003 (3) Adjust the cross fitting [1] assembly to align to the check valve [3] with the elbow [4] and restrictor [6] with elbow [7]. NOTE: The 'green' colored tube (bleed air line) connects to the check valve, while the 'silver' colored tube (balance line) connects to the restrictor (orifice). (a) Tighten the swivel nut at each elbow to 133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m). SUBTASK 29-09-04-420-004 (4) Tighten the swivel nut [9] and coupling nut [8] at the pressure relief valve and adjacent hydraulic reservoir tubing to 427 in-lb (48.2 N·m) - 473 in-lb (53.4 N·m).

D. Post-Installation Leakage Check

SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-005 (1) Pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold duct. SUBTASK 29-09-04-790-001 (2) Use a solution of soap and water to check that no air leaks at the swivel nut connections on the cross fitting assembly. SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-006 (3) Depressurize the pneumatic cross manifold duct. SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-007 (4) If necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-09-04-860-008 (1) Set the FLT CONTROL A and FLT CONTROL B switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ON position.

(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-001 (2) Do these tasks to remove hydraulic power if supplied to the airplane: (a) For the main hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805 (b) For the standby hydraulic system, do this task: Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802 29-09-05 SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-002 WARNING YOU MUST REMOVE THE PRESSURE FROM THE PNEUMATIC DUCTS BEFORE YOU REMOVE A PNEUMATIC SYSTEM COMPONENT . SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-004 (1) Make sure the hydraulic reservoirs have been depressurized before you remove the pressure relief valve [1] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802). (a) Remove the dust cap on the air charging valve then slowly unscrew the swivel nut to release any residual air pressure. (b) Reinstall dust cap and tighten swivel nut. SUBTASK 29-09-05-020-002 (3) Loosen the swivel nuts on each end of the pressure relief valve [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-05-020-003 (4) Remove the pressure relief valve [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-05-020-004 (5) Remove the unions [2] and packings [3] (o-rings) from the pressure relief valve [1]. (a) Discard the packings [3] but keep the unions [2] for re-installation. SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-001 (6) Install plugs/caps to the tube ends and pressure relief valve ports.

29-09-05-400-801Pressure Relief Valve - Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-801

Task Description

3. Pressure Relief Valve - Installation (Figure 201)

A. References

Reference Title 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201)

B. Consumable Materials

C. Expendables/Parts

D. Location Zones

E. Pressure Relief Valve Installation

SUBTASK 29-09-05-020-005 (1) Remove the plugs/caps from the tube ends and pressure relief valve ports. SUBTASK 29-09-05-640-001 (2) Lightly lubricate the new packings [3] (o-rings) with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-002 (3) Install the packings [3] (o-rings) and the unions [2] to the pressure relief valve ports, and tighten. SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-003 (4) Install the pressure relief valve [1] and tighten the swivel nuts. NOTE: The 'IN-OUT' flow arrow on the pressure relief valve [1] must point away from the adjacent cross fitting assembly. The inlet side of the pressure relief valve [1] is adjacent to the cross fitting assembly. The outlet side of the pressure relief valve [1] is adjacent to the APU fuel line shroud drain mast tubing. SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-004 (5) Install the clamp [6], washers [5], and screws [4] to the pressure relief valve [1]. F. Post-Installation Leakage Check SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-005 (1) Pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold duct. SUBTASK 29-09-05-790-001 (2) Use a solution of soap and water to check that no air leaks at the swivel nut connection on the inlet side of the pressure relief valve [1]. SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-006 (3) Depressurize the pneumatic cross manifold duct. SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-007 (4) If necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802

SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-013 (1) Disconnect the hydraulic tube [1] from the orifice assembly [13]. SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-014 (2) Disconnect the pneumatic supply lines [10] from the pressurization module [2]. 29-09-06 SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-015 (3) Install caps on the pneumatic supply lines [10] and the tube [1] and the ports in the pressurization module [2]. SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-016 (4) Remove the pressurization module [2]: (a) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [4] from the pressurization module [2]. (b) Remove the pressurization module [2] from the airplane. SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-017 (5) Remove these parts from the pressurization module [2] if they are necessary for the replacement pressurization module [2]: (a) Remove the orifice assembly [13] from the pressurization module [2]. 1) Remove the nut [14], retainer [18], packing [17], backup ring [16], and packing [15]. 2) Make a record of position of the packing [17], backup ring [16], and packing [15]. 3) Discard the backup ring [16] and packings [15] [17]. (b) Remove the plug [7] and packing [11] from the test port [12]. 1) Discard the packing [11]. (c) Remove the reducers [9] and packings [7] from the pneumatic supply ports. 1) Discard the packings [7].

29-09-06-400-805Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module - Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-805

Task Description

3. Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module - Installation Figure 401

A. Consumable Materials

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 29-09-06-640-004 (1) Install these parts in the new pressurization module [2] if they are not installed: (a) The orifice assembly [13]: 1) Lubricate the threads, packing [17], packing [15], and backup ring [16] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153. 2) Install the nut [14], retainer [18], packing [17], backup ring [16], and packing [15] on the orifice assembly [13]. 3) Install the orifice assembly [13] on the pressurization module [2] but do not tighten it. (b) The plug [7] in the test port [12]: 1) Lubricate the packing [11] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153. 2) Install the packing [11] on the plug [7]. 3) Install the plug [7] on the pressurization module [2]. 4) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912. (c) The reducers [9] in the pneumatic supply ports: 1) Lubricate the packing [8] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153. 2) Lubricate the threads of the reducers [9] with primer, C00259. 3) Install the packing [8] on the reducers [9]. 4) Install the reducers [9] in the pressurization module [2]. SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-015 (2) Install the pressurization module [2]: (a) Put the pressurizationmodule [2] in its position. (b) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] to attach the pressurizationmodule [2] to the bracket. 29-09-06 SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-016 (3) Remove the caps from the hydraulic tube [1] and the pneumatic supply lines [10]. SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-017 (4) Connect the hydraulic tube [1] to the orifice assembly [13]: (a) Adjust the orifice assembly [13] until you can connect the hydraulic tube [1]. (b) Tighten the orifice assembly [13]. SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-018 (5) Connect the pneumatic supply lines [10] to the pressurization module [2].

D. Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module Installation Test

SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-019 (1) Remove the DO-NOT-USE tag from the connector for the ground pneumatic air. SUBTASK 29-09-06-790-008 (2) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module - Leak Check, TASK 29-09-06-790-803.

SUBTASK 29-09-06-390-002 (4) Apply RTV 162 adhesive, A00363, around the filter cap [6].

29-11-00-170-801Hydraulic System A or B Flushing ATA 29 · Task 170-801

Task Description

7. Hydraulic System A or B Flushing

A. General

(1) This procedure flushes the hydraulic system after you replace a hydraulic pump because of a mechanical malfunction, or if you find metal contamination in the filter. (2) If the airplane experiences repeated failures of a pump at one location, there may be debris in the case drain line, case drain hose, case drain hose quick-disconnect or case drain filter module check valve contamination that cannot be flushed by accomplishing this procedure. Careful examination, cleaning, or replacement of the case drain hose or quick-disconnect may be required. 29-11-00 (3) If contamination from a damaged pump is found when you flush the hydraulic system, then it is recommended to do these steps: NOTE: Operator experience shows that a new filter can become plugged by debris that remains in the hydraulic system after a mechanical failure. A plugged filter can cause hydraulic fluid to bypass the filter element and allow debris to circulate in the system. Debris that bypasses the filter can cause a premature failure of a new hydraulic pump. (a) Examine the case drain line and hoses for contamination or blockage. (b) If contamination or blockage is found, clean or replace the case drain line. (c) Replace the case drain filter element again, at the next maintenance opportunity following one week of normal operation. (d) Replace all the filter elements in the system at the next maintenance opportunity following two months of normal operation. (4) If the contamination of the hydraulic fluid is from a chemical source, replace the fluid and the filter elements.

B. References

(a) Replace the filter element of the case drain filter module for the Engine Driven Pump (EDP). These are the tasks: EDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-51-000-801, EDP Case Drain Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-51-400-801. (b) Replace the filter element of the case drain filter module for the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP). These are the tasks: EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-41-000-801, EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-41-400-801. (c) Replace the filter element of the pressure module. These are the tasks: Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-71-000-802, Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-71-400-802. (d) Replace the filter element of the return module. These are the tasks: Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801, Return Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-61-400-801. (e) Replace the PTU Pressure Filter Element. These are the tasks: PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801, PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation, TASK 29-22-21-400-802. SUBTASK 29-11-00-170-002 (4) Inspect the EMDP acoustic filter for metal particle contamination, do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning, TASK 29-11-00-100-801. SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-006 (5) Inspect the Hydraulic Systems A and B Return Filter Element for metal particle contamination, do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Return Filter Element - Inspection, TASK 29-11-61-200-801. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY DURING THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (6) To pressurize the applicable hydraulic system with the pump that you replaced, do one of these steps: (a) Do this task: Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803. (b) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-804. 29-11-00 SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-017 (7) Operate all the systems that operate with the hydraulic pressure (but not the landing gear) not less than six times at a fast rate. NOTE: To flush hydraulic system tubing from the pump to the pressure and case drain filters, the preferred method is to run the flaps, and spoilers. To flush hydraulic system tubing from the pump to the return filters, the preferred method is to run the thrust reversers, aileron and spoiler, rudder, and elevator. (a) Examine the case drain line and hoses for contamination or blockage. (b) If contamination or blockage is found, clean or replace the case drain line. SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-018 (8) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-11-00-900-002 (10) Do these steps to replace the pressure, return, and case drain filter elements that has a relation to the pump with the mechanical malfunction: NOTE: Filter elements are replaced again to make sure that contaminates are removed from the hydraulic system. NOTE: Do only the steps necessary to replace the filter elements for the applicable pumps. (a) Replace the filter element of the case drain filter module for the EDP . These are the tasks: EDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-51-000-801, EDP Case Drain Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-51-400-801. (b) Replace the filter element of the case drain filter module for the EMDP . (c) Replace the filter element of the pressure filter module. (d) Replace the filter element of the return filter module. E. Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning

SUBTASK 29-11-00-000-001 (1) Do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal, TASK 29-11-27-000-801. SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-002 (2) To clean the hydraulic systems A and B EMDP acoustic filter assembly [4], do these steps: CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU CUT THE LOCK WIRE FROM THE FILTER ASSEMBLY . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE OF THE BARREL AND HEAD ASSEMBLY . (a) Remove and discard lockwires from the acoustic filter assembly [4]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CAREFULLY DRAIN HYDRAULIC FLUID INTO A SUITABLE CONTAINER. CAREFULLY CLEAN, DRY , AND DISPOSE OF ALL LEAKAGE. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAUSES DAMAGE TO RUBBER, COPPER, PLASTICS, PAINTS, AND MANY OTHER MATERIALS. (b) Use the wrenching flats on the barrel and head to disassemble the acoustic filter assembly [4]. (c) Remove and discard the packing [1], packing [2], and backup rings [3]. (d) Use solvent, B00184, or equivalent to flush all surfaces and let air dry. (e) Examine all surfaces, packing grooves, and threads for defects or contamination. (f) Install the new packing [1], new packing [2], and new backup rings [3] (TASK 20-10-31-400-801). CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY ALIGN AND INSTALL BACKUP RINGS. EXTRUSION AND LEAKS CAN OCCUR IF YOU DO NOT CORRECTLY INSTALL BACKUP RINGS. 1) Make sure that the spiral-cut teflon backup rings [3] are aligned and installed correctly. (g) Apply hydraulic fluid, D50122, to the threads of the filter head and filter barrel. (h) Assemble the acoustic filter assembly [4]. 29-11-00 (i) Tighten the filter head to 480 in-lb (54 N·m) - 540 in-lb (61 N·m). 1) Use the wrenching flats on the filter barrel and filter head. (j) Apply tamper-proof putty/lacquer, G51751, to the thread connections on the end fittings on the filter head and filter barrel. (k) Install MS20995C20 lockwires, G50225, with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 29-11-00-420-004 (3) If the end fittings are removed from the aluminum filter housing for end fitting O-ring seal replacement, reinstall the end fittings as follows (TASK 20-50-11-910-801): (a) Tighten 3/8-inch end of AFP2814-1006 or 32345F1006 steel elbow at the upper end of the filter housing to 170 in-lb (19.2 N·m). (b) Tighten 1/2-inch MS21902-8 steel union at the lower end of the filter housing to 280 in-lb (31.6 N·m). SUBTASK 29-11-00-170-001 (4) Replace the EMDP if the acoustic filter assembly [4] contains metal particles: (a) Do this task: Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal, TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001. (b) Do this task: Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation, TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001. (c) Flush the hydraulic lines between the acoustic filter assembly [4] and the EMDP . SUBTASK 29-11-00-420-006 (5) Install the acoustic filter assembly [4], do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation, TASK 29-11-27-400-801.

Task Description

9. Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Inspection and Corrosion Repair (Figure 204 or Figure 205 or Figure 206)

A. General

(1) This task includes general inspection and repair hydraulic systems A and B electric motor-driven pump (EMDP) acoustic filter parts procedure.

B. References

Reference Title 29-11-27-000-801 Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-27-400-801 Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation (P/B 401)

C. Consumable Materials

D. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-047 (1) Remove the hydraulic systems A and B electric motor-driven pump (EMDP) acoustic filter assembly. Do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal, TASK 29-11-27-000-801. (2) Do these steps to clean the acoustic filter, for proper visual inspection: (a) Flush all surfaces with solvent, B00184 or equivalent. (b) If a hard substance cannot be removed from the unit, use an emery cloth, G00744 in slow motions until the hard substance is removed.

E. Inspection of the Acoustic Filter Assembly

SUBTASK 29-11-00-210-004 (1) Do a visual check as follows: (a) For wear, exposed aluminum, dents, scratches, corrosion and cracks. (b) For obstructions on the flow tube assembly. (c) For bad threads on the barrel and head assemblies. 29-11-00 F. Repair Procedures for Damage on the Flow Tube SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-003 (1) If the flow tube is damaged or corroded discard the unit or return to manufacturer for evaluation and or replacement. NOTE: Do not attempt to repair. (2) If the flow tube is not damaged, then make sure that the three long holes (flow passages) are clean and clear of foreign objects. (3) To clean the flow tube do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning, TASK 29-11-00-100-801.

G. Repair Procedures for Damage on the Barrel

SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-004 CAUTION DO NOT REPAIR MORE THAN 5 PERCENT ON THE MATERIAL, IF THE REPAIR IS MORE THAN 5 PERCENT , REPLACE THE ASSEMBLY . NOTE: Make sure that the acoustic filter components are protected at all time of procedure. (1) If the damage or corrosion on the barrel exceeds the damage limit of 0.010 in. (0.254 mm) or is within the NO REWORK area, discard the unit or return to manufacturer for evaluation and or replacement. NOTE: Do not attempt to repair. (2) For scratches, dents, blistering, flaking, corrosion, and pitting that will require removal of less then 0.010 in. (0.254 mm) of material, do these steps: (a) Cover all openings to avoid contamination. (b) Remove damage by lightly sanding or with a lathe. NOTE: Use abrasive paper, G50339, or emery cloth, G00744 to remove damage. (c) Do a Liquid Penetrant, G51208 test to make sure that there are no cracks on the barrel. (d) Clean the repair and apply a protective film with Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079 or coating, C00851 to the repair.

H. Repair Procedure for Damage on the Head

SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-005 (1) If the damage or corrosion on the head exceeds the damage limit of 0.004 in. (0.102 mm) or is within the NO REWORK area, discard the unit or return to manufacturer for evaluation and or replacement. NOTE: Do not attempt to repair. (2) For scratches, dents, blistering, flaking, corrosion, and pitting that will require removal of less then 0.004 in. (0.102 mm) of material, do these steps: (a) Cover all openings to avoid contamination. (b) Remove damage by lightly sanding. NOTE: Use abrasive paper, G50339, or emery cloth, G00744 to remove damage. (c) Do a Liquid Penetrant, G51208 test to make sure that there are no cracks on the head. (d) Clean the repair and apply a protective film with Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079 or coating, C00851 to the repair. 29-11-00

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-11-00-420-007 (1) Install the hydraulic systems A and B electric motor-driven pump (EMDP) acoustic filter assembly. Do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation, TASK 29-11-27-400-801.

SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-021 CAUTION DO NOT OPERATE SYSTEM A OR B HYDRAULIC PUMPS FOR MORE THAN TWO MINUTES WITHOUT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS. THE NO. 1 (FOR SYSTEM A) AND NO. 2 (FOR SYSTEM B) FUEL TANKS MUST HAVE A MINIMUM OF 250 GALLONS (1675 POUNDS/760 KILOGRAMS) OF FUEL IN THEM. IF THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS, THE HYDRAULIC FLUID WILL BECOME TOO HOT . (1) Make sure that the No. 1 and No. 2 fuel tanks each have 250 gallons (1675 lb (760 kg)) of fuel in them. SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-022 (2) Make sure that the flap control lever is in the FLAP UP position. 29-11-00 SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-055 (3) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 15 C01081 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 1 A 16 C01085 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 2 SUBTASK 29-11-00-010-006 (4) To get access to the P91 and P92 panels, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-024 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (5) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP NOTE: The Standby Hydraulic Pump circuit breaker is located behind the P92 front panel. SUBTASK 29-11-00-210-002 (6) Make sure that the supply shutoff valves for the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) are open. SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-025 (7) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are full. (a) To fill them, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 29-11-00-860-026 (8) If it is necessary, pressurize the hydraulic reservoirs. 29-11-00 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL THE HYDRAULIC COMPONENTS WHEN POWER IS ON. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY DURING THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . E. Operational Test of the Hydraulic System A and B

SUBTASK 29-11-00-710-001 (1) Do the operational test of the hydraulic systems A and B: (a) Make sure that the four LOW PRESSURE lights, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are on. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL THE HYDRAULIC COMPONENTS WHEN POWER IS ON. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY DURING THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (b) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP): 1) For hydraulic system A, set the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 switch to the ON position. 2) For hydraulic system B, set the HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 switch to the ON position. 3) Make sure that the HYD P indicator for the applicable hydraulic system becomes stable between 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) and 3200 psig (22,063 kPa). NOTE: The HYD P indicator is shown on the P2 pilots center panel or P9 panel display. 4) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light goes off. (c) Set the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 or HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 to the OFF position. 1) Operate the rudder until the hydraulic pressure is zero. 2) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light comes on. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL THE HYDRAULIC COMPONENTS WHEN POWER IS ON. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY DURING THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (d) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP): 1) For hydraulic system A, set the HYD PUMPS A ENG 1 switch to the ON position. 2) For hydraulic system B, set the HYD PUMPS B ENG 2 switch to the ON position. 3) Motor the applicable engine to pressurize hydraulic system A or B, do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00. 4) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light goes off. 29-11-00 5) Make sure that the HYD P indicator for the applicable hydraulic system becomes stable between 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) and 3200 psig (22,063 kPa). NOTE: The HYD P indicator is shown on the P2 pilots center panel or P9 panel display. 6) Set the HYD PUMPS A ENG 1 or HYD PUMPS B ENG 2 to the OFF position. 7) Operate the rudder until the hydraulic pressure is zero. 8) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light comes on. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. (4) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system with the electric motor driven pump (TASK 29-11-00-860-803): (a) For hydraulic system A, set the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 switch to the ON position. (b) For hydraulic system B, set the HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 switch to the ON position. (c) Make sure that the HYD P indicator for the applicable hydraulic system becomes stable between 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) and 3200 psig (22,063 kPa). NOTE: The HYD P indicator is shown on the P2 pilots center panel or P9 panel display. (d) Set the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 or HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 to the OFF position. 29-11-00 (e) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ELEC 1 or ELEC 2) comes on when the pressure is between 1100 psig (7584 kPa) and 1500 psig (10,342 kPa). SUBTASK 29-11-00-720-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL THE HYDRAULIC COMPONENTS WHEN POWER IS ON. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY DURING THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Motor the applicable engine to pressurize hydraulic system A or B, do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00. (a) For hydraulic system A, set the HYD PUMPS A ENG 1 switch to the ON position. (b) For hydraulic system B, set the HYD PUMPS B ENG 2 switch to the ON position. (c) Make sure the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ENG 1 or ENG 2) goes off. (d) Make sure that the HYD P indicator for the applicable hydraulic system becomes stable between 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) and 3200 psig (22,063 kPa). NOTE: The HYD P indicator is shown on the P2 pilots center panel or P9 panel display. (e) Set the HYD PUMPS A ENG 1 or HYD PUMPS B ENG 2 to the OFF position. (f) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ENG 1 or ENG 2) comes on. NOTE: If it is necessary, operate the flight controls to remove pressure from the hydraulic systems. (g) Set the HYD PUMPS A ENG 1 or HYD PUMPS B ENG 2 back to the ON position. (h) Make sure the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ENG 1 or ENG 2) goes off. (i) Make sure the HYD P indicator for the applicable hydraulic system becomes stable between 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) and 3200 psig (22,063 kPa). (j) Make sure there is no hydraulic leakage at the EDP .

29-11-00-200-801Hydraulic Fluid - Check ATA 29 · Task 200-801

Task Description

2. Hydraulic Fluid - Check (Figure 601)

A. General

(1) You must supply clean bottles which will hold the fluid samples. If you do not do this, it is possible that the fluid samples will not be correct. (2) Supply clean sample bottles from a satisfactory laboratory, or a vendor (for example, Fisher, Catalog #02-893-5D or equivalent). Use non-powdered gloves to prevent contamination during the sampling procedure. Remove the bottle cap immediately before you collect the sample. Put the cap face down on a clean (lint-free, dirt-free) surface during sampling. (a) If the first sample has a high particle count, you can sample the hydraulic fluid again with the hydraulic fluid check task. NOTE: This will show, if there was contamination during the sampling procedure and could prevent replacing all the systems fluid. (3) You must get one hydraulic fluid sample from each hydraulic reservoir. (4) A polyethylene bottle (500ml), STD-1104, or a capacity 2 ounces, with polyethylene screw cap and seal, glass bottle, STD-1105, can be used to collect the hydraulic fluid. NOTE: The glass bottle is shown as an alternate choice because low quality polyethylene containers can allow organic contaminants to pass into the oil sample and affect the test results. Polyethylene containers made from high grade PE, especially those obtained from the hydraulic fluid supplier, are permitted for use.

SUBTASK 29-11-00-160-001 (1) Clean the drain valve on the reservoir with cotton wiper, G00034. (a) Make sure that there is no contamination in the port before you drain the fluid. SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-008 (2) Remove and discard the lockwire or safety cable from the reservoir drain valve. SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-001 WARNING HYDRAULIC FLUID, BMS 3-11, CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. IF YOU GET THE HYDRAULIC FLUID ON YOUR SKIN, FLUSH YOUR SKIN WITH WATER. IF YOU GET HYDRAULIC FLUID IN YOUR EYES, FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. IF YOU EAT OR DRINK THE HYDRAULIC FLUID, GET MEDICAL AID. (3) Open the reservoir drain valve to supply a smooth flow of fluid into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-002 (4) Drain a minimum of 1 pt (0.5 l) of hydraulic fluid before you get a sample. SUBTASK 29-11-00-020-001 (5) Remove the cap from the bottle and put the cap face down on a clean (lint-free dirt-free) surface. SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-003 (6) Do these steps to fill the bottle: NOTE: It is only necessary to get samples from the A and B hydraulic systems. The standby hydraulic system reservoir gets fluid from the hydraulic system B. (a) Put the bottle in the fluid flow but do not touch the reservoir drain valve. (b) When the bottle is full, remove it from the fluid flow. NOTE: Do not close the reservoir drain valve, while the bottle is in the fluid flow. This will prevent contamination of the sample. 29-11-00 SUBTASK 29-11-00-420-002 (7) Install the cap on the bottle. SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-005 (8) Close the reservoir drain valve. SUBTASK 29-11-00-420-003 (9) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the reservoir drain valve with double twist method. SUBTASK 29-11-00-930-001 (10) Write this data on the bottle: (a) Airplane model (b) Airplane number (c) Hydraulic system number (d) Date (e) Location. NOTE: After you remove a fluid sample from the hydraulic reservoir, do an analysis of the fluid properties which show in Table 601. If one or more of the fluid properties is more than the limit or is not in the specified range, replace a sufficient quantity of the fluid until the property is less than the limit. Follow local procedures to find the quantity of fluid that must be replaced. NOTE: If petroleum contamination is found, immediate hydraulic fluid replacement is required (TASK 29-00-00-900-801). (b) Method (b) - the heat exchanger replaced with new part/spliced to existing heat exchanger tubes: 1) Cut the remaining hydraulic tubes at recommended locations (Figure 402), based on ease of accessibility (TASK 20-10-51-400-808). 2) Remove and keep support clamps. 3) Remove the cut tube sections. NOTE: Keep the cut tube sections to refer to make replacement tube sections. Use the same aluminum tubing as the sections.

H. Heat Exchanger Installation

SUBTASK 29-11-04-650-003 WARNING OBEY THE PRECAUTIONS FOR PURGING AND FUEL TANK ENTRY . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE PRECAUTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Prepare the fuel tank before you go into it (TASK 28-11-00-910-802). SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-001 (2) Put the heat exchanger [1] through the main tank access door. NOTE: Put the end of the heat exchanger [1] with the inlet port [11] and outlet port [13] in first. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-002 (3) T emporarily install washer [6], washer [4], washer [3], bolt [2], and nut [5]. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-003 (4) T emporarily install washer [6], washer [15], bonding jumper [14], washer [3], bolt [16], washer [4], and nut [5]. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-004 (5) If it is necessary, install an additional washer [15] to provide clearance between the bonding jumper [14] and heat exchanger [1]. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-006 (6) Measure the clearance between the washer [6] and the heat exchanger [1]. (a) If the clearance is more than 0.007 in. (0.178 mm), add additional washer [6] to fill the clearance. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-007 (7) Tighten the nuts [5]. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-008 (8) Install the washers [8], washers [9], bolts [7], and nuts [10]. SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-009 (9) Connect the inlet port [11] and the outlet port [13] of the new heat exchanger to the hydraulic lines by performing one of the following methods, shown in Figure 404 and Figure 405 (based on which action was taken during heat exchanger removal). (a) Method (a) hydraulic tubes to new heat exchanger replaced with new tubes (Figure 405 and Figure 407). 29-11-04 1) Install new tube runs of the same part number with new externally swaged fittings (TASK 20-10-51-400-808). a) Obey the requirements for bonding and grounding/faying surfaces on permaswage bulkhead penetration fittings during part installation (TASK 29-11-55-400-801). b) Keep sufficient tube clearances (TASK 20-10-51-200-801). c) Use the kept support clamps and fasteners. CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO DISCONNECT OR CONNECT TUBES. IF YOU DO NOT USE A WRENCH ON EACH SIDE OF THE CONNECTION, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES CAN OCCUR. 2) Connect the hydraulic lines to the penetration fittings (TASK 29-11-55-400-801). (b) Method (b) new heat exchanger spliced to existing hydraulic heat exchanger tubes (Figure 406 and Figure 408). 1) Cut replacement sections (tube splices) from new tubes of the correct part numbers or make tube splices from 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) diameter and 0.035 in. (0.889 mm) wall thickness, 6061-T6 aluminum tubing (AMS4083). a) Use removed (kept) tube sections as the pattern. b) Use the replacement tubes to connect the new heat exchanger to the remaining tube sections (TASK 20-10-51-300-805). NOTE: There is one recommended location for the heat exchanger (hydraulic system A) in the left wing and two optional locations (for inlet port [11] and outlet port [13]) for the heat exchanger (hydraulic system B) in the right wing. 2) Install the tube splices (TASK 20-10-51-400-808). a) Obey the electrical resistance requirements for permaswage fittings during part installation/swaging (TASK 20-10-51-760-801). b) Keep sufficient tube clearances (TASK 20-10-51-200-801). c) Use the kept support clamps and fasteners. SUBTASK 29-11-04-410-004 (10) Install the fuel tubes before the heat exchanger removal and replacement (TASK 28-22-15-400-801). (a) Obey the electrical bonding requirements. SUBTASK 29-11-04-940-001 (11) Make sure that you remove all of the tools, unwanted parts, and unwanted objects from the wing fuel tank. 29-11-04

I. Heat Exchanger Installation Test

SUBTASK 29-11-04-210-001 (1) Make sure that the bonding jumper [14] is installed from the heat exchanger [1] to the structure inside the tank. NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. SUBTASK 29-11-04-860-011 28-AWL-10: CDCCL (2) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the structure and the heat exchanger [1] (SWPM 20-20-00). NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 28-AWL-10: CDCCL (b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0050 ohm (5.0 milliohms) or less. NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs). NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. SUBTASK 29-11-04-760-003 28-AWL-10: CDCCL (3) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the hydraulic heat exchanger and each externally swaged hydraulic tube fitting (SWPM 20-20-00). NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs). NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 28-AWL-10: CDCCL (b) Make sure the electrical bonding resistance is 0.00041 ohm (0.41 milliohm) or less. NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs). NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. 29-11-04 SUBTASK 29-11-04-760-002 28-AWL-10: CDCCL (4) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the hydraulic tubes and the externally swaged hydraulic tube fittings (SWPM 20-20-00). NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs). NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 28-AWL-10: CDCCL (b) Make sure the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0005 ohm (0.5 milliohm) or less. NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs). NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10. NOTE: The externally swaged fittings connecting the hydraulic tubes to the heat exchanger are reducer unions. The heat exchanger side is a 0.625 in. (15.9 mm) and the hydraulic tube side is a 0.50 in. (12.7 mm). SUBTASK 29-11-04-211-001 (5) Do a check of the seals on the bulkhead fittings. (a) If it is necessary, replace the fillet seal on the bulkhead fittings on the outside of the tank. 1) Use sealant, A02315, to apply the fillet seal. (b) If it is necessary, replace the full bodied fillet seal on the inside of the tank. 1) Use sealant, A00436, to apply a fillet seal. SUBTASK 29-11-04-410-003 (6) Do these steps to install the applicable access doors: (a) Install the applicable main tank access doors: Number Name/Location 532AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 632AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 1) Do this task: Main T ank Access Door Installation, TASK 28-11-11-400-801. (b) Install the applicable main tank inner access doors: Number Name/Location 532BZ Main T ank Inner Access at Rib 6 632BZ Main T ank Inner Access at Rib 6 1) Do this task: Main T ank Inner Access Door Installation, TASK 28-11-11-400-804. 29-11-04 SUBTASK 29-11-04-860-005 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (7) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00768 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS B Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00767 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS A SUBTASK 29-11-04-860-006 (8) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or TASK 29-09-00-860-807). SUBTASK 29-11-04-860-008 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . CAUTION DO NOT OPERATE THE EMDP FOR MORE THAN 2 MINUTES UNLESS THE APPLICABLE FUEL TANK HAS A MINIMUM OF 1675 LBS (760 KG) OF FUEL IN IT . IF YOU OPERATE THE EMDP FOR 2 MINUTES WITHOUT FUEL IN THE TANK, LET THE RESERVOIR GO BACK TO AMBIENT TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU CONTINUE WITH THE TEST . IF YOU CONTINUE TO OPERATE THE EMDP , THE HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN BECOME TOO HOT . (9) Pressurize the hydraulic system with the applicable Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) (TASK 29-11-00-860-803). SUBTASK 29-11-04-780-001 (10) After some minutes, remove hydraulic pressure (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). 29-11-04 SUBTASK 29-11-04-010-002 (11) Remove the applicable main tank access doors: (Main T ank Access Door Removal, TASK 28-11-11-000-801) Number Name/Location 532AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 532BZ Main T ank Inner Access at Rib 6 632AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 632BZ Main T ank Inner Access at Rib 6 SUBTASK 29-11-04-790-001 (12) Make sure that there is no hydraulic fluid leakage at the hydraulic lines or from the heat exchanger [1]. (a) Repair leakage if it is necessary.

Task Description

2. Hydraulic systems A and B Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) Depressurization Solenoid Valve - Operational Check NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) Each engine has one engine-driven pump located on the forward side of the Accessory Gear Box (AGB) at the 3 o'clock position. (2) The Engine 1 and Engine 2 engine-driven pumps are the same. (3) The hydraulic hose connections have self-sealing disconnects to prevent leakage of hydraulic fluid and to keep air out of the hydraulic system. (4) For this procedure, the hydraulic systems A and B engine-driven pump will be referred to as the hydraulic pump.

B. References

Reference Title 12-12-00-610-801 Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing (P/B 301) 29-09-00-860-801 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-807 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 71-00-00-700-810-F00 Test 2 - Dry Motor Leak Test (P/B 501) 71-00-00-700-819-F00 Stop the Engine Procedure (Usual Engine Stop) (P/B 201) 71-00-00-700-821-F00 Dry Motor the Engine (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 410 Subzone - Engine 1 420 Subzone - Engine 2

D. Depressurization Solenoid Valve Operational Check

SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-037 (1) Do this task: Test 2 - Dry Motor Leak Test, TASK 71-00-00-700-810-F00. SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-038 (2) For engine1, make sure that the safety tag is removed and this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 15 C00779 HYD SYS ENG PUMP DEPRESS VALVE 1 29-11-11 SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-039 (3) For engine2, make sure that the safety tag is removed and this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 17 C00780 HYD SYS ENG PUMP DEPRESS VALVE 2 SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-043 (4) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or TASK 29-09-00-860-807). SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-044 (5) Make sure that all hydraulic pumps are not operating. SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-040 (6) Make sure that the flight control switches, on the P5 flight control panel, are set to the OFF position. SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-045 (7) Make sure that the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, is in the ON position. SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-046 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (8) Dry-motor the applicable engine to pressurize the hydraulic system (TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00). (a) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure becomes stable between 2800 psi (19,305 kPa) to 3200 psi (22,063 kPa). NOTE: You can view the hydraulic pressure, for the applicable system, on the display unit for the engine display. SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-047 (9) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable engine, to the OFF position until the hydraulic pressure decreases to 200 psi (1379 kPa) or less. NOTE: To accelerate pressure decay, it is acceptable to exercise flight controls to relieve residual, high pressure as long as safety precautions are observed. SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-048 (10) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, to the ON position and make sure that the pressure becomes stable between 2800 psi (19,305 kPa) to 3200 psi (22,063 kPa). SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-041 (11) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, to the OFF position and let the system pressure decrease to 200 psi (1379 kPa) or less. NOTE: To accelerate pressure decay, it is acceptable to exercise flight controls to relieve residual, high pressure as long as safety precautions are observed. SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-049 (12) Stop the engine (TASK 71-00-00-700-819-F00). 29-11-11 SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-050 (13) Make sure that the pump does not have a hydraulic leak.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-051 (1) Set the flight control switches, on the P5 flight control panel, to the ON position. SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-052 (2) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, to the ON position. SUBTASK 29-11-11-840-005 (3) Remove power from the applicable hydraulic system (TASK 29-11-00-860-805). SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-042 (4) If it is necessary, service the system A and B reservoirs (TASK 12-12-00-610-801).

(1) Set the WXR switch on the Weather Radar (WXR) control panel, to TEST . SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-013 (2) Use one of the following tasks to supply electrical power: NOTE: Do not use external ground power to do this test. (a) Do this task: Supply IDG Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-817. 1) Prepare the engine for operation (TASK 71-00-00-700-818-F00). (b) Do this task: Supply APU Generator Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-815. 1) Prepare the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) for operation (TASK 49-11-00-860-801). SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-014 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES DURING THE LEAK CHECK. THE AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATOR FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 29-11-21 (WARNING PRECEDES) CAUTION DO NOT OPERATE THE SYSTEM A OR THE SYSTEM B EMDP FOR MORE THAN 2 MINUTES IF THE NO. 1 OR THE NO. 2 FUEL TANK (RESPECTIVELY) CONTAINS LESS THAN 250 GALLONS (1675 POUNDS, 760 KG) OF FUEL. YOU MUST LET THE RESERVOIR TEMPERATURE DECREASE TO AMBIENT TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU OPERATE THE PUMP AGAIN. DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Set the ELEC 1 and ELEC 2 HYD PUMP switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ON position. SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-015 (5) Set the ENG 1 and ENG 2 HYD PUMP switches, on the P5 panel, to the OFF position (if the engines are in operation). SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-016 (6) Set the FLT CONTROL and SPOILER system A and B switches, on the P5 panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 29-11-21-710-001 (7) Make sure that the HYD P indicator for each hydraulic system, on the P2 pilots center panel, or the P9 panel display, is 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) - 3200 psig (22,063 kPa). SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-017 (8) Set the applicable switch, on the P5 panel, to the OFF position to remove electrical power from the system A EMDP: (a) The GEN 2 switch (if the engine is your supply of electrical power). (b) The right APU GEN switch (if the APU is your supply of electrical power). SUBTASK 29-11-21-710-002 (9) Make sure that the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 panel, comes on. SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-018 (10) Set the GEN 2 or the right APU GEN switch back to the ON position. SUBTASK 29-11-21-710-003 (11) Make sure that the HYD PUMPS A ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE light goes out. SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-019 (12) Set the applicable switch, on the P5 panel, to the OFF position to remove electrical power from the system B pump: (a) GEN 1 (if the engine is your supply of electrical power). (b) The left APU GEN switch (if the APU is your supply of electrical power). SUBTASK 29-11-21-710-004 (13) Make sure that the HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 panel, comes on. SUBTASK 29-11-21-860-020 (14) Set the GEN 1 or the left APU GEN switch back to the ON position. 29-11-21 SUBTASK 29-11-21-710-005 (15) Make sure that the HYD PUMPS B ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE light goes out.

E. Prepare for Installation

SUBTASK 29-11-31-210-001 (1) Make sure that the surfaces of the system A reservoir [3] are clean. SUBTASK 29-11-31-210-002 (2) Make sure that unwanted material does not get in the reservoir [3]. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-001 (3) If it is necessary to install components on the replacement reservoir [3], do these steps: (a) Install the drain valve [17]: 1) Remove the caps from the ports on the reservoir [3]. 2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153 on the new packing [7]. 3) Install the packing [7] in the groove of the flange of the drain valve [17]. 4) Put the drain valve [17] on the flange. 5) Install the bolts [15] and washers [16]. 6) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the two bolts [15] with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or TASK 20-10-44-400-802). 29-11-31 7) Put the drain valve handle in the CLOSED position. 8) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the drain valve [17] and on the other two bolts [15] with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or TASK 20-10-44-400-802). (b) Install the reducer [14], reducer [20], and disconnect coupling [8]. 1) Remove the caps from the ports on the reservoir [3]. 2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153 to the new packing [10], new packing [13], new packing [19], reducer [14], reducer [20], and disconnect coupling [8]. 3) Install the packing [10], packing [13], packing [19], reducer [14], reducer [20], and disconnect coupling [8] in the reservoir ports. (c) Do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Transmitter/Indicator Installation, TASK 29-33-12-400-801. F. Hydraulic System A Reservoir Installation SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-002 (1) Put the hydraulic reservoir [3] in its mounting position. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-003 (2) Install the bolts [1] and washers [2]. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-004 (3) Remove the caps from the electrical conector [6], fluid quantity transmitter, hydraulic line [11], hydraulic line [12], hydraulic line [18] and the ports on the reservoir [3]. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-005 (4) Connect the electrical conector [6] to the fluid quantity transmitter. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-006 (5) Connect hydraulic line [11] and hydraulic line [18] to the reservoir [3]. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-015 (6) Tighten the B-nuts on hydraulic line [11] and hydraulic line [18] to a torque of 450 ±23 in-lb (50.8 ±2.6 N·m). SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-016 (7) Connect hydraulic line [12] to the reservoir [3]. SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-017 (8) Tighten the B-nut on hydraulic line [12] to a torque of 750 ±38 in-lb (84.7 ±4.3 N·m). SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-007 (9) Connect the reservoir pressurization line [4]. SUBTASK 29-11-31-860-008 (10) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name D 5 C01359 DISPLAY DEU 1 PRI F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 11 C01360 DISPLAY DEU 2 PRI 29-11-31

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 29-11-41-840-001 (1) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-11-41-010-005 (2) To get access to the P91 and P92 panels, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 29-11-41-860-001 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (3) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name F 3 C00882 ELEC HYD PUMP SYS B Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 3 C00881 ELEC HYD PUMP SYS A SUBTASK 29-11-41-860-002 (4) Remove pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-11-41-860-013 (5) Disconnect the supply line at the system A Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) quick-disconnect or the system B EMDP quick-disconnect, as applicable. F. EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-018 (1) If it is necessary, remove the filter module, do this task: EMDP Case Drain Filter Module Removal, TASK 29-11-41-000-802. NOTE: The filter element can be removed from the filter module after removing the module from the airplane. 29-11-41 SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-001 (2) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the filter bowl [13] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801 or TASK 20-10-44-000-802). SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-017 (3) Remove the filter bowl [13] from the filter head. (a) Put a container below the filter bowl [13] to catch any hydraulic fluid. SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-002 (4) Remove the filter element [12] from the case drain filter assembly [6]. SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-003 (5) Remove the packing [9] from the filter element [12]. (a) Discard the packing [9]. SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-004 (6) Remove the packing [11] and backup rings [10] from the filter head. NOTE: An o-ring pick, COM-7293, may be used to remove the packing. (a) Make sure that you do not scratch the filter head. (b) Discard the packing [11]. (c) If you find a crack, damage or deformation on any backup rings [10], discard the part. SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-008 (7) Check the EMDP for condition every time when the filter is removed (EMDP Case Drain Filter Element and Bowl Inspection, TASK 29-11-41-200-801). SUBTASK 29-11-41-140-001 (8) Clean the filter bowl [13].

29-11-41-700-801EMDP Case Drain Filter - Metal Contamination Check ATA 29 · Task 700-801

Task Description

6. EMDP Case Drain Filter - Metal Contamination Check (Figure 401)

A. General

(1) Do this task if you found unacceptable metal contamination in the case drain filter for the EMDP .

B. References

Reference Title 29-11-00-100-801 Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning (P/B 201) 29-11-21-000-801-001 Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-21-400-801-001 Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation (P/B 401) 29-11-27-000-801 Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-27-400-801 Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation (P/B 401) 29-11-71-000-802 Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-71-400-802 Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation (P/B 401) 29-22-00-730-801 Power Transfer Unit (PTU) System Test (P/B 501) 29-22-11-000-801 Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal (P/B 401) 29-22-11-400-801 Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation (P/B 401) 29-22-21-020-801 PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal (P/B 401) 29-22-21-400-802 PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation (P/B 401)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 29-11-41-170-001 (1) Flush the hydraulic lines between the case drain filter and the hydraulic pump. SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-004 (2) Look for metal contamination in the pressure filter for the EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-71-000-802. (a) If you find metal contamination, do these steps: 1) Flush the hydraulic lines between the pressure filter and the EMDP . 2) Install a new pressure filter element. These are the tasks: Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-71-000-802, Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-71-400-802. 3) Install a new EMDP . 29-11-41 These are the tasks: Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal, TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001, Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation, TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001. (b) If you do not find metal contamination in the pressure filter of the EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-71-400-802. SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-005 (3) Look for metal contamination in the acoustic filter for the EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal, TASK 29-11-27-000-801. (a) If you find metal contamination, do these steps: 1) Clean the acoustic filter, do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning, TASK 29-11-00-100-801. 2) Install a new EMDP . These are the tasks: Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal, TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001, Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation, TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001. (b) If you do not find metal contamination in the acoustic filter, do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation, TASK 29-11-27-400-801. SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-006 (4) If the acoustic filter and the pressure filter for the EMDP do not have metal contamination, then do these steps: (a) Look for metal contamination in the pressure filter for the PTU, do this task: PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801. (b) If you find metal contamination, do these steps: 1) Flush the hydraulic lines between the pressure filter and the PTU. 2) Install a new PTU pressure filter element. These are the tasks: PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801, PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation, TASK 29-22-21-400-802. 3) Install a new PTU. These are the tasks: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal, TASK 29-22-11-000-801, Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation, TASK 29-22-11-400-801. (c) If the pressure filter for the PTU does not have metal contamination, do these steps: 1) Do this task: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) System Test, TASK 29-22-00-730-801. 2) If the PTU does not operate correctly, replace the PTU. These are the tasks: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal, TASK 29-22-11-000-801, Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation, TASK 29-22-11-400-801.

29-11-41-200-801EMDP Case Drain Filter Element and Bowl Inspection ATA 29 · Task 200-801

Task Description

2. EMDP Case Drain Filter Element and Bowl Inspection

A. References

Reference Title 29-11-00 P/B 501 HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS A AND B - ADJUSTMENT/TEST 29-11-00-170-801 Hydraulic System A or B Flushing (P/B 201) 29-11-21-000-801-001 Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-21-400-801-001 Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation (P/B 401) 29-11-41-000-801 EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-41-400-801 EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Installation (P/B 401)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

C. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-015 (1) Do this task: EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-41-000-801.

D. Inspection

SUBTASK 29-11-41-211-001 (1) Examine the filter element, the filter bowl, and the fluid in the filter bowl for metal contamination. (a) If you find a small quantity of metal particles that have equal dimensions, do these steps: NOTE: It is not necessary to replace a pump if the quantity of metal particles is small and they have equal dimensions. The filter can have more particles during initial operation of a new pump while mating parts wear away small surface defects. It is not necessary to replace the pump if more small particles are found at the next filter change after installation of a new pump. 1) Replace the filter element. 2) Do this task: HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS A AND B - ADJUSTMENT/TEST , PAGEBLOCK 29-11-00/501. 3) Examine the filter again at the next scheduled filter change interval. (b) If you find a large quantity of small metal particles, large metal particles that are not of equal dimensions, or a large quantity of steel particles, do these steps: NOTE: A large quantity of small metal particles, or large metal particles that are not of equal dimensions, can be an indication of an unsatisfactory pump. The particles are usually bronze mixed with a small quantity of steel. A large quantity of steel particles is an indication of unsatisfactorily worn bearings. 29-11-41 1) Replace the pump at the next maintenance opportunity (TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001 and TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001). 2) Write down the results of the filter inspection and give them to the pump overhaul facility. NOTE: The filter inspection results can be used as an aid to find the condition of the pump. A pump with an unsatisfactory bearing can pass the functional test and be returned to service with no fault found. Giving the filter inspection data to the overhaul facility can prevent the return of an unsatisfactory pump to service. 3) Replace the filter element. CAUTION FLUSH THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO REMOVE METAL CONTAMINATION. IF A LARGE QUANTITY OF METAL CONTAMINATION STAYS IN THE LINES, THE FILTER CAN BECOME BLOCKED. A BLOCKED FILTER CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PUMP . (c) If you will remove a pump because of metal contamination in the filter, flush the hydraulic lines and replace the applicable filter elements (TASK 29-11-00-170-801). SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-007 (2) Inspect the filter element for damages. (a) Discard and replace the filter element if damages are found.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-11-41-420-013 (1) Do this task: EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-41-400-801.

29-11-51-000-801EDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-801

Task Description

2. EDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal (Figure 401) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-019 CAUTION DO NOT DISCONNECT THE QUICK-RELEASE FITTING FOR THE HYDRAULIC CASE DRAIN-LINE AT THE SUPPORT BEAM FOR THE STRUT FAN COWL. A DISCONNECTED CASE DRAIN LINE WITH A QUICK-RELEASE FITTING CAN CAUSE TO INCORRECT INSTALLATION. AN INCORRECTLY INSTALLED QUICK-RELEASE FITTING CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE HYDRAULIC PUMP . (1) Do not disconnect the hydraulic case drain line quick release fitting at the strut fan cowl support beam. NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the hydraulic case drain line quick release fitting. A check valve is installed on the downstream side of the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) case drain filter module. The check valve will prevent hydraulic fluid loss when the EDP case drain filter element is removed. SUBTASK 29-11-51-000-002 (2) If it is necessary, you can remove the filter element after you remove the case drain filter module, do these tasks: 29-11-51 • EDP Case Drain Filter Module Removal, TASK 29-11-51-000-802 • EDP Case Drain Filter Module Installation, TASK 29-11-51-400-802. SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-021 (3) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the filter bowl [8] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801 or TASK 20-10-44-000-802). SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-001 (4) Remove the filter bowl [8] from the filter head. (a) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a container. SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-012 (5) Remove the filter element [7] from the filter head. SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-013 (6) Remove the packing [6] from the filter element [7]. (a) Discard the packing [6]. SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-014 (7) Remove the packing [10] and backup rings [5] from the filter head. NOTE: You can use an o-ring pick, COM-7293, to remove the packing. (a) Discard the packing [10]. (b) If you find a crack, damage or deformation on a backup ring [5], discard the part. SUBTASK 29-11-51-210-007 (8) Do the check of the EDP case drain filter element and bowl for condition every time that the filter is removed (TASK 29-11-51-200-801). SUBTASK 29-11-51-160-001 (9) Clean the filter bowl [8].
