D. Inspection

SUBTASK 29-11-51-211-001 (1) Examine the filter element, the filter bowl, and the fluid in the filter bowl for metal contamination. (a) If you find a small quantity of metal particles that have equal dimensions, do these steps: NOTE: It is not necessary to replace a pump if the quantity of metal particles is small and they have equal dimensions. The filter can have more particles during initial operation of a new pump while mating parts wear away small surface defects. It is not necessary to replace the pump if more small particles are found at the next filter change after installation of a new pump. 1) Replace the filter element. 2) Do an operational test of the engine driven pump (TASK 29-11-00-700-801). 3) Examine the filter again at the next scheduled filter change interval. 29-11-51 (b) If you find a large quantity of small metal particles, large metal particles that are not of equal dimensions, or a large quantity of steel particles, do these steps: NOTE: A large quantity of small metal particles, or large metal particles that are not of equal dimensions, can be an indication of an unsatisfactory pump. The particles are usually bronze mixed with a small quantity of steel. A large quantity of steel particles is an indication of unsatisfactorily worn bearings. 1) Replace the pump at the next maintenance opportunity (TASK 29-11-11-000-801-001 and TASK 29-11-11-400-801-001). 2) Write down the results of the filter inspection and give them to the pump overhaul facility. NOTE: The filter inspection results can be used as an aid to find the condition of the pump. A pump with an unsatisfactory bearing can pass the functional test and be returned to service with no fault found. Giving the filter inspection data to the overhaul facility can prevent the return of an unsatisfactory pump to service. 3) Replace the filter element. CAUTION FLUSH THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO REMOVE METAL CONTAMINATION. IF A LARGE QUANTITY OF METAL CONTAMINATION STAYS IN THE LINES, THE FILTER CAN BECOME BLOCKED. A BLOCKED FILTER CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PUMP . (c) If you will remove a pump because of metal contamination in the filter, flush the hydraulic lines and replace the applicable filter elements (TASK 29-11-00-170-801). SUBTASK 29-11-51-210-005 (2) Inspect the filter element for damages. (a) Discard and replace the filter element if damages are found.

(b) Install a cap in the hydraulic line and bulkhead fitting [1] to prevent contamination. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-002 (2) If it is necessary, remove the support clamps or blocks from the tube you will remove. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-003 (3) Cut the tube attached to the applicable bulkhead fitting [1] with the 3000 psi tube repair kit, SPL-541. 29-11-55 (a) Make sure that the cut is in a straight section of tubing. NOTE: This will make sure that the fitting and swage tool connect for installation. SUBTASK 29-11-55-680-001 (4) Use a oil resistant container, STD-203, to catch hydraulic fluid that drains from the cut line. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-005 (5) Install a cap in the cut hydraulic line. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-006 (6) Do these steps to remove the applicable bulkhead fitting [1]. (a) Remove the sealant from around the bulkhead fitting [1], spar [2] and bolts [4]. (b) Remove the collars [5] from the bolts [4] (SRM 51-40-02-0G-0). (c) Remove the bulkhead fitting [1] from the spar [2]. (d) Remove and discard the O-ring [3]. (e) If it is necessary, remove the union [6] from the bulkhead fitting [1]. Keep for the installation procedure.

SUBTASK 29-11-55-410-003 (1) Install the applicable main fuel tank access panel: (TASK 28-11-11-400-801) 29-11-55 Number Name/Location 532AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 632AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 NOTE: The fuel tank must be closed before power can be applied to the airplane. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (2) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00768 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS B Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00767 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS A SUBTASK 29-11-55-860-006 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . CAUTION DO NOT OPERATE THE ELECTRIC MOTOR-DRIVEN PUMP (EMDP) MORE THAN TWO MINUTES UNLESS THE FUEL TANKS CONTAIN MORE THAN 1675 LBS (761 KG) OF FUEL. IF THE PUMP OPERATES FOR TWO MINUTES WITHOUT THE FUEL IN THE TANK, LET THE RESERVOIR GO BACK TO AMBIENT TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU OPERATE THE PUMP AGAIN. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Do this task to pressurize the applicable hydraulic system: Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803. SUBTASK 29-11-55-720-001 (4) Operate the controls for the hydraulic system that contains the repaired hydraulic line. NOTE: This helps to remove air from the hydraulic system. 29-11-55 SUBTASK 29-11-55-860-007 CAUTION DO NOT OPERATE THE ELECTRIC MOTOR-DRIVEN PUMP (EMDP) MORE THAN TWO MINUTES UNLESS THE FUEL TANKS CONTAIN MORE THAN 1675 LBS (761 KG) OF FUEL. IF THE PUMP OPERATES FOR TWO MINUTES WITHOUT THE FUEL IN THE TANK, LET THE RESERVOIR GO BACK TO AMBIENT TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU OPERATE THE PUMP AGAIN. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (5) After some minutes, remove hydraulic power from the applicable system (TASK 29-11-00-860-805). NOTE: If the heat exchanger for the hydraulic system is above the surface of the fuel, it can become too hot. SUBTASK 29-11-55-860-008 (6) Release pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (1) For the bulkhead fitting [1] to the rear spar [2] outside the fuel tank resistance, do these steps: (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550 (b) Make sure that the electrical fay surface bond resistance between the bulkhead fitting [1] and the rear spar [2] outside the fuel tank is 0.0010 ohm (1.0 milli-ohm) or less (SWPM 20-20-00). (c) If the resistance is above the specified value, loosen the bulkhead fittings to repair the electrical bond: 1) Do this task: Bulkhead Fittings - Separate From Rear Spar to Repair Electrical Bond, TASK 29-11-55-300-801. 29-11-55 SUBTASK 29-11-55-760-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE BONDING RESISTANCE IS LESS THAN THE LIMITS. (2) For the bulkhead fitting [1] to the hydraulic tube inside the fuel tank resistance, do these steps: (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550 (b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance between the hydraulic tube in the fuel tank and bulkhead fitting [1] is 0.00050 ohm (0.50 milli-ohm) or less. (c) Remove and install a new hydraulic tube to the bulkhead fitting [1], if the resistance is above the specified value.

G. Separate the Bulkhead Fittings from the Rear Spar

SUBTASK 29-11-55-100-001 CAUTION DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON EQUIPMENT . IF HYDRAULIC FLUID GETS ON EQUIPMENT , IMMEDIATELY CLEAN IT FROM THE EQUIPMENT . HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) During this procedure, if you get hydraulic fluid on any equipment, surfaces or cables, clean it off immediately, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803 SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-007 CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO DISCONNECT OR CONNECT TUBES. IF YOU DO NOT USE A WRENCH ON EACH SIDE OF THE CONNECTION, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES CAN OCCUR. (2) Disconnect the hydraulic tube B-nuts attached to the inlet and outlet bulkhead fittings [2] on the outside of the fuel tank. (a) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a oil resistant container, STD-203. (b) Install plugs in the disconnected hydraulic tubes [1] and caps on the bulkhead fittings [2] to prevent contamination. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-008 (3) If necessary, remove any support clamps or blocks from the disconnected hydraulic tubes [1] to allow the bulkhead fittings [2] to be pulled away from the rear spar [3]. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-009 (4) Do these steps to loosen the bulkhead fittings [2] from the rear spar [3]: (a) Remove the sealant from the bulkhead fittings [2], two sides of the rear spar [3], and bolts [4] with the scraper, STD-6401, or scraper, STD-11161. NOTE: Remove sealant with cutting tools or spatulas made from fiberglass, hardwood, or plastic. Use only metal tools for the sealant removal on metal structures. NOTE: The unions can stay installed on their bulkhead fittings. (b) Remove the collars [6] from the bolts [4] (SRM 51-40-02-0G-0). SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-010 (5) Remove the fuel tubes adjacent to hydraulic tubes in the fuel tank if necessary to get access to the heat exchanger and related hydraulic tubing, do this task: Fuel Line, Fitting and Coupling Removal, TASK 28-22-15-000-801. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-011 (6) Disconnect the clamps [7] from the tank structure, on the hydraulic lines from the heat exchanger to the bulkhead fittings. 29-11-55 SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-012 (7) Do these steps to loosen the applicable heat exchanger [8] from the attach points in the main fuel tank: (a) Remove the nuts [9], washers [10], washers [11], and bolts [12] from the heat exchanger [8] at two diagonal locations. (b) Remove the nut [13], washer [14], washer [15], bolt [16], and washer [17] that attach the heat exchanger [8] to the tank. (c) Remove the nut [13], washer [14], bolt [18], washer [15], bonding jumper [19], washer [20], and washer [17] that attach the heat exchanger [8] to the tank. (d) Keep a record of the number of washers [17] for installation. SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-013 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE CAREFUL WHEN YOU DISCONNECT THE BULKHEAD FITTINGS FROM THE REAR SPAR. YOU MUST KEEP THE O-RINGS SERVICEABLE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , YOU MUST REPLACE THE BULKHEAD FITTINGS. (8) Carefully move the heat exchanger [8] and connected hydraulic tubing aft to disconnect the bulkhead fittings [2] from the rear spar [3].

H. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 29-11-55-100-002 (1) Clean unwanted material from the O-ring [21] with cotton wiper, G00034. SUBTASK 29-11-55-200-001 (2) Examine the condition of the O-ring [21] on each bulkhead fitting [2]. (a) If the O-ring [21] is damaged, replace the bulkhead fitting [2], do these tasks: • Bulkhead Fitting Removal, TASK 29-11-55-000-801 • Bulkhead Fitting Installation, TASK 29-11-55-400-801. SUBTASK 29-11-55-160-008 (3) Do the prepare for installation steps of task: Bulkhead Fitting Installation, TASK 29-11-55-400-801. (a) Carefully move the O-ring [21] if necessary during cleaning. SUBTASK 29-11-55-160-009 (4) Prepare the heat exchanger, bonding jumper terminal, and washer below the terminal for category 1 bonding (unsealed) (SWPM 20-20-00 and 20-20-10). SUBTASK 29-11-55-160-005 (5) Clean the heat exchanger, bonding jumper terminal, and washer below the terminal with cotton wiper, G00034, and alcohol, B00065. 29-11-55 SUBTASK 29-11-55-370-008 WARNING DO NOT GET THE ALODINE SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK- AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (6) Manually apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C50315, to any bare aluminum.

I. Installation of the Bulkhead Fittings and Heat Exchanger to Repair Electrical Bonds

SUBTASK 29-11-55-420-005 (1) In the tank, move heat exchanger [8] and connected hydraulic tubing forward to connect the bulkhead fittings [2] with the rear spar [3]. SUBTASK 29-11-55-420-006 (2) Install the bulkhead fittings [2] to the rear spar [3] (TASK 29-11-55-400-801). (a) Ignore the steps for cut tubes and the step to Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition. (b) Do the Bulkhead Fitting Installation Test after the heat exchanger [8] is installed. SUBTASK 29-11-55-420-026 (3) Install the heat exchanger [8] to the tank structure (TASK 29-11-04-400-801). (a) Ignore the steps for cut tubes and the step to Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition. (b) Do the Bulkhead Fitting Installation Test and Heat Exchanger Installation Test at the same time.

J. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

(1) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00768 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS B 29-11-55 Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00767 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS A SUBTASK 29-11-55-410-010 (2) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 29-11-55-860-026 (3) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-11-55-410-007 (4) Install the applicable main fuel tank access panel: (TASK 28-11-11-400-801) Number Name/Location 532AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 632AB Main T ank Access Door - Wing Station 216 SUBTASK 29-11-55-410-008 (5) Close the applicable access panel: Number Name/Location 551DB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Lube Actuator & MLG Beam Outboard Attach Pin Access Panel 651DB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Lube Actuator & MLG Beam Outboard Attach Pin Access Panel SUBTASK 29-11-55-650-010 (6) Refuel the fuel tank, do this task: Pressure Refuel Procedure, TASK 12-11-00-650-802. (a) Make sure that there are no fuel leaks at the rear spar [3] and bulkhead fittings [2]. SUBTASK 29-11-55-610-005 (7) Fill the applicable hydraulic system reservoir, if necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

E. Return Filter Element Installation

SUBTASK 29-11-61-640-001 (1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [14] and to new packing [16]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-018 (2) Install the new packing [16] into the grove of the filter element [15]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-003 (3) Install the new packing [14] on the head of the filter bowl [11]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-004 (4) Install the filter element [15] in the filter head assembly. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-005 (5) Install the filter bowl [11] in the filter head. NOTE: For system A return filter module only, position the clamp so that the opening of the clamp is inboard and the nut is accessible, providing maximum clearance from the system A Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) pressure hose. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-007 (7) Install the nut [10] on the clamp [9]. 29-11-61 RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-284; AIRPLANES WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY FROM PALL AEROPOWER CORPORATION SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-008 (8) Tighten the nut [10] on the clamp [9] to 120 in-lb (13.56 N·m) - 144 in-lb (16.27 N·m). RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-284; AIRPLANES WITH V-BAND CLAMP FILTER MODULE SUBTASK 29-11-61-860-003 (10) If it is necessary, push the differential pressure indicator. SUBTASK 29-11-61-600-001 (11) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED FILTER MODULE F. Return Filter Element Installation SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-010 (1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [14] and to new packing [16]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-017 (2) Install the new packing [16] into the grove of the filter element [15]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-011 (3) Install the new packing [14] on the head of the filter bowl [11]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-012 (4) Install the filter element [15] in the filter head assembly. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-013 (5) Do these steps to install the filter bowl [11] in the filter head: (a) Rotate the lock ring [9] and move it up to the engaged position. (b) Install the filter bowl [11]. (c) Tighten the filter bowl [11] by hand. NOTE: The lock ring engages the filter head when the filter bowl is tight. SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-014 (6) If it is necessary, push the differential pressure indicator. 29-11-61-000-802Return Filter Module Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-802

Task Description

4. Return Filter Module Removal (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 12-40-00-100-801 Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane (P/B 201) 12-40-00-100-803 Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane (P/B 201) 20-10-44-000-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Removal (P/B 401) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-808 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-6569 Container - Hydraulic Fluid Resistant, 1 Gallon (3.8 Liter)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 29-11-61-840-002 (1) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable system (TASK 29-11-00-860-805). SUBTASK 29-11-61-860-007 (2) Release the pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808).

E. Return Filter Module Removal

SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-008 (1) Do this step to remove system A filter module [8]: RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED FILTER MODULE (a) Remove the lockwire on the reducer [6] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3 (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). RYR ALL 29-11-61 (b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [3], hydraulic line [4] and disconnect the port 1 union [5] from the hydraulic line. SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-009 (2) Do this step to remove system B filter module [13]: RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED FILTER MODULE (a) Remove the lockwire on the plug [17] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3 (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). RYR ALL (b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [12], and disconnect the union [5] from the port 1 hydraulic line. SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-010 (3) Install plugs in the disconnected hydraulic lines. SUBTASK 29-11-61-680-001 (4) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a 1 gallon (3.8 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-6569. SUBTASK 29-11-61-160-001 (5) If it is necessary, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803. SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-011 (6) Remove the bolts [1] and washers [2]. SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-012 (7) Remove the filter module [8] and/or filter module [13].

29-11-61-400-802Return Filter Module Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-802

Task Description

5. Return Filter Module Installation (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 12-12-00-610-801 Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing (P/B 301) 20-10-44-400-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation (P/B 401) 29-09-00-860-801 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-807 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201)

29-11-61

29-11-61

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

E. Return Filter Module Installation

SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-002 (1) Install the filter module [8] and/or filter module [13]. (a) If packings and fittings are not installed on the filter module, do these steps: 1) For system A filter module [8]: a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packings [7], unions [5] and reducer [6]. b) Install the new packing [7] and union [5] in port 1, new packing [7] and reducer [6] in port 2, and new packing [7] and union [5] in port 3. RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED FILTER MODULE c) Install the lockwire on the reducer [6] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3 (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). RYR ALL 2) For system B filter module [13] do these steps: a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packings [7], unions [5] and port 2 plug [17]. b) Install the new packing [7] and union [5] in port 1, new packing [7] and union [5] in port 3, and new packing [7] and plug [17] in port 2. RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED FILTER MODULE c) Install lockwire on the plug [17] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3 (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). RYR ALL (b) Attach the filter module [8] or filter module [13] to the structure with bolts [1] and washers [2]. (c) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic lines. (d) For the filter module [8] connect the hydraulic line [3] to port 3, connect the hydraulic line [4] to port 2 and connect the union [5] in port 1 to the hydraulic line. (e) For the filter module [13] connect the hydraulic line [12] to port 3, and connect the union [5] in port 1 to the hydraulic line. (f) For the system A filter module [8] only: 1) Loosen the nut [10] from the clamp [9]. 2) Position the clamp [9] so that the opening of the clamp is inboard and the nut [10] is accessible, providing the maximum clearance from the system A Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) pressure hose. 3) Tighten the nut [10] on the clamp [9] to 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) - 144 in-lb (16.3 N·m) (for filter assembly from Aircraft Porus Media manufacturer), or 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) (for filter assembly from Purolator manufacturer). 29-11-61 F. Return Filter Module Installation Test SUBTASK 29-11-61-600-002 (1) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 29-11-61-860-008 (2) Pressurize the applicable reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or TASK 29-09-00-860-807). SUBTASK 29-11-61-860-009 (3) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system (TASK 29-11-00-860-801). SUBTASK 29-11-61-790-002 (4) Examine the filter module [8], filter module [13], and hydraulic line connections for leaks.

29-11-61-210-801Inspection of the Differential Pressure Indicator of the A and B System Return Filter Modules ATA 29 · Task 210-801

Task Description

2. Inspection of the Differential Pressure Indicator of the A and B System Return Filter Modules Figure 601 NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. References

Reference Title 29-11-61-000-801 Return Filter Element Removal (P/B 401) 29-11-61-400-801 Return Filter Element Installation (P/B 401)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 29-11-61-010-001 (1) Get access to the main wheel well. SUBTASK 29-11-61-210-001 (2) Do a visual check of the differential pressure indication of the A and B system return filter modules. (a) Make sure that the red differential pressure indicator is not visible. (b) If red differential pressure indicator is visible, do this task: Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801, Return Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-61-400-801.

29-11-61-200-801Hydraulic Systems A and B Return Filter Element - Inspection ATA 29 · Task 200-801

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

C. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-017 (1) Remove the return filter element (Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801).

D. Inspection

SUBTASK 29-11-61-210-002 (1) Examine the filter element to make sure that it is not filled with unwanted material and it does not have damage. (a) If the filter element is not serviceable, discard and replace the filter element.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-016 (1) Install the return filter element (TASK 29-11-61-400-801).

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-001 (1) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B 29-11-71 Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-002 (2) Depressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-003 (3) For the Hydraulic System A, do this step: (a) To get access to the P91 and P92 panels, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (b) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00767 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS A F 3 C00881 ELEC HYD PUMP SYS A SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-004 (4) For the Hydraulic System B, do this step: (a) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 15 C01081 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 1 A 16 C01085 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 2 (b) To get access to the P91 and P92 panels, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door 29-11-71 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (c) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00768 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS B F 3 C00882 ELEC HYD PUMP SYS B F. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Removal SUBTASK 29-11-71-440-001 (1) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-001 (2) Disconnect the applicable hydraulic system electrical connectors from the pressure switches and the pressure transducer: (a) Hydraulic System A: Disconnect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [2], and electrical connector [3]. (b) Hydraulic System B: Disconnect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [2], electrical connector [3], and electrical connector [31]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-002 (3) Disconnect the applicable hydraulic system hydraulic lines, do this task: Flareless Tubing Assembly Removal, TASK 20-10-51-000-801. (a) Hydraulic System A: Disconnect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30]. (b) Hydraulic System B: Disconnect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-680-001 (4) Drain hydraulic fluid into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. SUBTASK 29-11-71-160-001 (5) Do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-003 (6) Install plugs to the hydraulic lines on the applicable hydraulic system to prevent contamination and damage: 29-11-71 (a) Hydraulic System A: Install plugs to the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30] to prevent contamination or damage. (b) Hydraulic System B: Install plugs to the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27] to prevent contamination or damage. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-021 (7) Remove the lockwire between applicable plug and pressure module [57]: (a) For the Hydraulic System A, remove the lockwire between the plug [6] and pressure module [57]. (b) For the Hydraulic System B, remove the lockwire between the plug [32] and pressure module [57]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-004 (8) Remove the unions and the plug from the pressure module [57] on the applicable hydraulic system: (a) Hydraulic System A: Remove the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], union [28], and plug [6] from the pressure module [57]. 1) Discard the packing [7], packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and packing [29]. (b) Hydraulic System B: Remove the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and plug [32] from the pressure module [57]. 1) Discard the packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and packing [33]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-001 (9) Install plugs in the open ports of the pressure module [57] to prevent contamination or damage. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-005 (10) Remove the bolt [4], bolt [14], washer [5], and washer [15]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-006 (11) Remove the pressure module [57].

SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-001 CAUTION DO NOT LET UNWANTED MATERIALS GO INTO THE PRESSURE MODULE OR THE HYDRAULIC LINES. DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Make sure that unwanted material does not go into the pressure module ports or the hydraulic lines. SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-001 (2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packings and to the threads of the plug and union for the applicable hydraulic system. (a) Hydraulic System A: Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [7], packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and packing [29] and to the threads of the plug [6], union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and union [28]. (b) Hydraulic System B: Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and packing [33] and to the threads of the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and plug [32]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-002 (3) Install the new packings on the plug and unions for the applicable hydraulic system. (a) For Hydraulic System A, do these steps: 1) Install the new packing [7] on the plug [6]. 2) Install the new packing [9] to the union [8]. 3) Install the new packing [12] on the union [11]. 29-11-71 4) Install the new packing [19] on the union [18]. 5) Install the new packing [23] on the union [22]. 6) Install the new packing [26] on the union [25]. 7) Install the new packing [29] on the union [28]. (b) For Hydraulic System B, do these steps: 1) Install the new packing [9] on the union [8]. 2) Install the new packing [12] on the union [11]. 3) Install the new packing [19] on the union [18]. 4) Install the new packing [23] on the union [22]. 5) Install the new packing [26] on the union [25]. 6) Install the new packing [33] on the plug [32]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-010-001 (4) If shipping plugs are in ports of the pressure module [57], remove them. SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-002 (5) Install the plug and unions in the pressure module [57] for the applicable hydraulic system. (a) Hydraulic System A: Install the plug [6], union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and union [28] in the correct ports of the pressure module [57]. 1) Tighten the union [8] to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m). 2) Tighten the union [11] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m). 3) Tighten the union [18] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m). 4) Tighten the union [22] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m). 5) Tighten the union [25] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m). 6) Tighten the union [28] to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m). NOTE: For installation torque values, refer to Standard Torque Values, TASK 20-50-11-910-801. (b) Hydraulic System B: Install the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and plug [32] in the correct ports of the pressure module [57]. 1) Tighten the union [8] to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m). 2) Tighten the union [11] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m). 3) Tighten the union [18] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m). 4) Tighten the union [22] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m). 5) Tighten the union [25] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m). (a) Hydraulic System A: Connect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30] to the pressure module [57]. 1) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [10] to 700 ±35 in-lb (79 ±4 N·m). 2) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [13] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m). 3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [20] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m). 4) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [24] to 900 ±45 in-lb (102 ±5 N·m). 5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [27] to 700 ±35 in-lb (79 ±4 N·m). 6) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [30] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m). (b) Hydraulic System B: Connect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27] to the pressure module [57]. 1) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [10] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m). 2) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [13] to 900 ±45 in-lb (102 ±5 N·m). 3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [20] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m). 4) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [24] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m). 5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [27] to 900 ±45 in-lb (102 ±5 N·m). 29-11-71-000-802Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-802

Task Description

4. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal (Figure 401) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) There is one pressure modules for each hydraulic system. Each pressure module has two filter assemblies, one filter is for the electric motor driven pump and the other filter is for the engine driven pump. The procedure to remove and install each filter is similar.

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-010 (1) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-011 (2) Depressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. F. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-016 (1) Remove the lockwire from the filter bowl [16]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-017 CAUTION PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . (2) Disconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose from the applicable hydraulic system reservoir (TASK 29-11-27-000-801). SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-008 (3) Remove the filter bowl [16]. (a) Put a container under the filter bowl [16] to catch any hydraulic fluid. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-009 (4) Remove the filter [47]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-160-002 (5) Clean the filter bowl [16]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-010 (6) Remove the packing [43], packing [45], backup rings [46], and backup ring [44]. (a) Discard the packing [43], packing [45], backup rings [46], and backup ring [44]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-004 (7) Use a dental mirror, STD-3907, to examine the filter [47] for metal contamination. (a) If the filter [47] for the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) contains metal contamination, do these tasks: • Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal, TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001 • Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation, TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001. 29-11-71 (b) If the filter [47] for the Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) contains metal contamination, do these tasks: • Hydraulic Systems A and B Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) Removal, TASK 29-11-11-000-801-001 • Hydraulic Systems A and B Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) Installation, TASK 29-11-11-400-801-001. (c) If metal contamination is found in the pressure filter, flush the hydraulic lines between the pressure module [57] and hydraulic pump that was removed. (d) If metal contamination is found in the EMDP pressure filter, examine the EMDP acoustic filter, do these tasks: • Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal, TASK 29-11-27-000-801 • Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation, TASK 29-11-27-400-801. SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-011 (8) Discard the filter [47].

E. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation

SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-002 (1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [45] and the new backup rings [46]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-007 (2) Install the new packing [45] and the new backup rings [46] in the groove in the pressure module [57]. (a) Make sure that you set the new packing [45] and the new backup rings [46] correctly or they can cause a leak. SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-003 (3) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [43] and the new backup ring [44]. 29-11-71 SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-008 (4) Install the new packing [43] and the new backup ring [44] in the groove at the top of the new filter [47] with the new packing [43] at the top. SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-004 (5) Lightly apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the threads of the filter bowl [16]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-610-002 (6) Fill the filter bowl [16] approximately one third full with hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-009 (7) Put the new filter [47] in the pressure module [57]. SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-010 (8) Torque the filter bowl [16] to 350 in-lb (39.5 N·m) - 375 in-lb (42.4 N·m). SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-011 (9) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, between the filter bowl [16] and pressure module [57] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-022 CAUTION PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . (10) Reconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose (TASK 29-11-27-400-801). F. Hydraulic System A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation Test SUBTASK 29-11-71-600-001 (1) If it is necessary to service the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-013 (2) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. 29-11-71 SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-014 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system with the applicable hydraulic pump for the installed filter element: NOTE: The hydraulic pressure module has one set of hydraulic circuits and filter for the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) and one more set for the Engine Driven Pump (EDP). You must use the correct pump to do the leakage check. (a) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-11-71-790-001 (4) Examine the pressure module [57] for leaks. SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-015 (5) Remove hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

Prepare for the Removal SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-006 (1) For the applicable engine, attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on engine start lever. 29-11-81 SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-007 (2) For the Engine 1, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-008 (3) For the Engine 2, open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-001 (4) Release the pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir. NOTE: The system A reservoir is connected to the Engine 1. The system B reservoir is connected to the Engine 2. (a) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-11-81-680-001 (5) Drain the applicable reservoir. (a) Put a 10 gallon (40 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-6908, under the applicable reservoir. (b) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the drain valve. (c) Open the drain valve at the bottom of the applicable reservoir and drain into a container. (d) When the hydraulic fluid is drained, close the drain valve. (e) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the reservoir drain valve with double twist method. SUBTASK 29-11-81-100-001 (6) If you get hydraulic fluid on the airplane, do the step that follows: (a) Do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803. SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-002 (7) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 18 C00348 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM SHUTOFF VALVE ENG 2 C 19 C00347 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM SHUTOFF VALVE ENG 1

EDP Supply Shutoff Valve Installation SUBTASK 29-11-81-640-001 (1) Lubricate the new packings [5] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, and put them in their positions on the shutoff valve [1]. SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-001 (2) Carefully put the shutoff valve [1] between the adapter flanges. 29-11-81 (a) Make sure that the packings [5] do not get damaged or move out of their positions when you install the shutoff valve [1]. SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-003 (3) Install the bolts [12], bolt [13], washers [2], and nuts [3]. NOTE: Bolts can be installed from either direction. SUBTASK 29-11-81-120-001 (4) Clean the contact surfaces of the hinge bracket and bonding jumper [6]. (a) Manually clean the surface of the hinge bracket (TASK 20-10-34-120-801). 1) Use an abrasive pad. 2) Move the pad in a circular movement while you press with your thumb. 3) Final clean the surface. WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE OR CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENVIRONMENT . REFER TO THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) AND THE LOCAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS. a) Use a new cotton wiper, G00034 (alternate: knit cotton wiper, G51293), soaked with solvent, B00062, or solvent, B00184. b) Rub dry with a clean cotton wiper. c) Continue to clean and dry the surfaces until the cotton wiper stays clean. (b) Manually clean the surfaces of the terminal of the bonding jumper [6] (TASK 20-10-34-110-802). SUBTASK 29-11-81-390-003 (5) Apply a layer of sealant, A50110, sealant, A50155, sealant, A50231, or sealant, A50296, to the threads and shank of the bolt [8] used to install the bonding jumper [6]. SUBTASK 29-11-81-390-004 (6) Apply a thin continuous layer of sealant, A50110, sealant, A50155, sealant, A50231, or sealant, A50296, to the mating surfaces of the bolt [8], washers [2], nut [3], and terminal of the bonding jumper [6]. SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-013 (7) Install the bolt [8], washers [2], bonding jumper [6], and nut [3]. NOTE: Bolt can be installed from either direction. NOTE: One washer each under nut, jumper, and bolt head. SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-014 (8) If it was removed, install the bonding jumper [6] onto the bonding lug of the shutoff valve [1]. (a) Clean the contact surfaces of the bonding lug and bonding jumper [6]. 1) Manually clean the surface of the bonding lug (TASK 20-10-34-120-801). a) Use an abrasive pad. b) Move the pad in a circular movement while you press with your thumb. c) Final clean the surface. 29-11-81 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE OR CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENVIRONMENT . REFER TO THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) AND THE LOCAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS. <1> Use a new cotton wiper, G00034 (alternate: knit cotton wiper, G51293), soaked with solvent, B00062, or solvent, B00184. <2> Rub dry with a clean cotton wiper. <3> Continue to clean and dry the surface until the cotton wiper stays clean. d) If it is necessary, manually apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, to the bonding lug surface. 2) Manually clean the surfaces of the terminal of the bonding jumper [6] (TASK 20-10-34-110-802). (b) Install the screw [9], washers [10], bonding jumper [6], and nut [11]. NOTE: Screw can be installed from either direction. NOTE: One washer each under nut, jumper, and screw head. (c) Apply sealant, A50110, sealant, A50231, or sealant, A50359, to fully cover the screw [9], washers [10], terminal of the bonding jumper [6], and nut [11]. SUBTASK 29-11-81-760-001 (9) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the terminal of the bonding jumper [6] and the following parts (SWPM 20-20-00): • the hinge bracket • the bonding lug on the shutoff valve [1] (if it was removed). (a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. (b) Make sure that the resistance is not more than 0.001 ohm (1.0 milliohm). SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-004 (10) Remove the protective cap from the electrical connector [4]. SUBTASK 29-11-81-210-001 (11) Examine the electrical connector [4] for corrosion. WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES AT AIRPORTS WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAIN POTASSIUM FORMATE IS USED. ALSO DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR IS PART OF A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT . (a) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03). (b) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-012 (12) Connect the electrical connector [4] to the shutoff valve [1]. NOTE: Corrosion inhibiting compound is applied to the exterior of the mated electrical connectors after the operational test is completed. 29-11-81 (a) Tighten the electrical connector [4] with your hand plus 1/8 turn. SUBTASK 29-11-81-710-001 (13) Do this task: EDP Supply Shutoff Valve Operational Test, TASK 29-11-81-710-802. SUBTASK 29-11-81-390-002 (14) Apply Ardrox AV25 compound, G50170, to the mated electrical connector [4] assembly completely until the compound drips from the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). (a) Do not remove the excess corrosion inhibiting compound.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-11-81-710-002 (1) Make sure that the hydraulic system is fully operational. (a) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. (b) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-012 (2) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 18 C00348 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM SHUTOFF VALVE ENG 2 C 19 C00347 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM SHUTOFF VALVE ENG 1 SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-013 (3) For the Engine 1, do the following step: 29-11-81 (a) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name B 8 C01103 ENGINE 1 START VALVE SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-014 (4) For the Engine 2, do the following step: (a) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00154 ENGINE 2 START VALVE SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-015 CAUTION DO NOT TURN THE FIRE HANDLE. IF YOU TURN THE FIRE HANDLE, THE EXTINGUISHING BOTTLES WILL RELEASE THEIR CONTENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. (5) Push the override button behind the fire handle for the applicable engine and pull the handle (on the P-8 engine and APU fire control panel). (a) Make sure that the shutoff valve operates by observing that the position indicator arm on the valve actuator moves from OPEN to CLOSED. NOTE: An indicator arm on the output shaft of the electrical actuator assembly aligns with the CLOSED and OPEN markings on the actuator nameplate to indicate the valve position. SUBTASK 29-11-81-860-016 (6) Push in the fire handle for the applicable engine. (a) Make sure that the shutoff valve operates by observing that the position indicator arm on the valve actuator moves from CLOSED to OPEN. (b) Examine the shutoff valve for leaks.

SUBTASK 29-11-91-860-005 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 17 C00780 HYD SYS ENG PUMP DEPRESS VALVE 2 B 15 C00779 HYD SYS ENG PUMP DEPRESS VALVE 1 SUBTASK 29-11-91-860-009 (2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name C 12 C01276 MASTER CAUTION ANNUNCIATOR CONT 2 E 10 C00328 OVERHEAD 5V SECONDARY F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5 F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 SUBTASK 29-11-91-010-003 (3) To get access to the P91 and P92 panels, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door 29-11-91 SUBTASK 29-11-91-860-001 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (4) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00768 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS B Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00767 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS A SUBTASK 29-11-91-010-001 (5) Get access to the electrical connectors on the back of the P5-8 hydraulic pumps module [1] on the P5 forward overhead panel: (a) Loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the P5 forward overhead panel in position and let the panel rotate downward. SUBTASK 29-11-91-020-001 (6) Remove the P5-8 hydraulic pumps module [1] from the P5 forward overhead panel as follows: (a) Disconnect the electrical connectors D642 and D2486 at the back of the hydraulic pumps module [1]. WARNING HOLD THE HYDRAULIC PUMPS MODULE WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE 1/4-TURN FASTENERS. IF THE MODULE FALLS, INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (b) Hold the hydraulic pumps module [1] in place and loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the hydraulic pumps module [1] to the P5 forward overhead panel. (c) Remove the hydraulic pumps module [1].

29-18-01-000-801Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-801

Task Description

2. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Removal (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 12-40-00-100-801 Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane (P/B 201) 12-40-00-100-803 Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-808 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201)

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-1154 Container - 5 Gallon (19 Liter)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Removal

SUBTASK 29-18-01-860-003 (1) Release the pressure from the reservoirs (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). SUBTASK 29-18-01-860-001 (2) Put the reservoir fill selector valve to the CLOSED position. SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-001 (3) Disconnect the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] from the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-680-001 (4) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. SUBTASK 29-18-01-160-001 (5) Clean the working area (TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or TASK 12-40-00-100-803). SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-001 (6) Install caps on the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] to prevent contamination or damage. SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-006 (7) If the replacement pump does not have unions in the inlet and outlet ports, remove the union [4], union [7], packing [3], and packing [6]. (a) Discard the packing [3] and packing [6]. 29-18-01 SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-002 (8) Install covers on the inlet and outlet ports of the reservoir manual fill pump [1] to prevent contamination or damage. SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-002 (9) Remove the bolts [8], washers [9] (under the bolthead), washers [10] (under the nut), and nuts [11]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-003 (10) Remove the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-007 (11) If it is necessary, remove the handle [12] from the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. (a) Remove the bolt [13], washer [14], washer [15], and nut [16].

29-18-01-400-801Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Installation ATA 29 · Task 400-801

Task Description

3. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Installation (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 12-12-00-610-801 Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing (P/B 301) 20-10-51-200-801 Tubing Clearances Check (P/B 401) SWPM 20-10-11 WIRING ASSEMBLY AND INSTALLATION CONFIGURATION

B. Consumable Materials

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Installation

SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-004 (1) Remove the covers from the inlet and outlet ports of the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-007 (2) If the replacement pump does not have unions already installed in the inlet and outlet ports, do these steps: (a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [3], new packing [6], union [4], and union [7]. (b) Install the packing [6] and union [7] in the inlet port and the packing [3] and union [4] in the outlet port. SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-013 (3) If removed, install the handle [12] on the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. (a) Install the bolt [13], washer [14], washer [15], and nut [16]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-004 (4) Put the reservoir manual fill pump [1] in its mounting position. SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-005 (5) Install the reservoir manual fill pump [1] with the bolts [8], washers [9] (under the bolthead), washers [10] (under the nut), and nuts [11]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-005 (6) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5]. SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-006 (7) Connect the hydraulic line [2] to the outlet port of the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. (a) Tighten the B-nut to 170 ±9 in-lb (19 ±1 N·m). SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-011 (8) Connect the hydraulic line [5] to the inlet port of the reservoir manual fill pump [1]. 29-18-01 (a) Tighten the B-nut to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m). SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-009 (9) Make sure that there is an adequate separation between tubing, wires and hoses (TASK 20-10-51-200-801). (a) If it is necessary, install clamps and spacers to maintain positive separation of wire bundles from hydraulic tubes (SWPM 20-10-11).

E. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Installation Test

SUBTASK 29-18-01-610-001 (1) Pump a small quantity of fluid through the reservoir manual fill pump [1] (TASK 12-12-00-610-801). SUBTASK 29-18-01-790-001 (2) Examine the reservoir manual fill pump [1] connections for leaks.

29-18-11-000-801Reservoir Fill Filter Module Removal ATA 29 · Task 000-801

Task Description

2. Reservoir Fill Filter Module Removal (Figure 401)

A. General

(1) In this procedure, the reservoir fill filter module is referred to as the "filter module", “filter assembly" and the reservoir fill filter element is referred to as the "filter element".

B. References

Reference Title 12-40-00-100-801 Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane (P/B 201) 12-40-00-100-803 Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-802 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201) 29-09-00-860-808 Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right

D. Reservoir Fill Filter Module Removal

SUBTASK 29-18-11-860-001 (1) Release pressure from the reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-18-11-020-001 (2) Remove the filter assembly [1]. (a) Put the reservoir fill selector valve to the CLOSED position. (b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] from the inlet and outlet ports of the fill filter module head. (c) Drain hydraulic fluid into a container. (d) Install caps on the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5]. (e) Install caps on the unions [4] of the filter head inlet and outlet ports. (f) If the new filter module does not have unions installed, remove unions [4] and packings [3]. (g) Discard the packings [3]. (h) Remove the filter module bolts [12] and washers [13]. 29-18-11 (i) Remove the reservoir fill filter assembly [1]. (j) If it is necessary, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.

Task Description

3. Reservoir Fill Filter Module Installation (Figure 401)

E. Reservoir Fill Filter Module Installation

SUBTASK 29-18-11-420-001 (1) Install the filter assembly [1]. (a) If packings [3] and unions [4] are not already installed on the filter head, do the following: 1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the packings [3] and the unions [4]. 2) Install packings [3] and unions [4] in the inlet and outlet ports of the filter module. (b) Install the filter assembly [1] to the structure with bolts [12] and washers [13]. (c) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5]. (d) Remove any caps or plugs that may be installed on the filter head inlet and outlet ports. (e) Connect the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] to the inlet and outlet ports of filter assembly [1]. 29-18-11 F. Reservoir Fill Filter Module Installation Test SUBTASK 29-18-11-790-001 (1) To service the hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. (a) Examine the filter assembly [1], hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] for leaks while you service the reservoir.

RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY FROM PALL AEROPOWER CORPORATION SUBTASK 29-18-11-020-002 (2) Remove the filter element [6]. (a) Put the reservoir fill selector valve to the CLOSED position. (b) Put a container below the filter bowl [9] to catch any hydraulic fluid. CAUTION PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . (c) Disconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose for the applicable hydraulic system. (d) Remove the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the filter head and filter bowl [9]. (e) Remove the filter bowl [9] with the filter element [6]. (f) Remove and discard the packing [8], packing [11], backup rings [7], and backup ring [10]. (g) Remove and discard the filter element [6]. (h) Clean the filter bowl [9]. 29-18-11 RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY FROM PTI TECHNOLOGIES SUBTASK 29-18-11-020-004 (3) Remove the filter element [17]. (a) Put the reservoir fill selector valve to the CLOSED position. (b) Put a container below the filter bowl [18] to catch any hydraulic fluid. CAUTION PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . (c) Disconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose for the applicable hydraulic system. (d) Remove the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the filter head and filter bowl [18]. (e) Remove the filter bowl [18] with the filter element [17]. (f) Remove and discard the packing [14], packing [11], backup rings [15], and backup ring [16]. (g) Remove and discard the filter element [17]. (h) Clean the filter bowl [18]. RYR ALL

D. Reservoir Fill Selector Valve Removal

SUBTASK 29-18-21-020-001 (1) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [15], hydraulic line [10] from the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. SUBTASK 29-18-21-680-001 (2) Put a container below the reservoir fill selector valve [6] to drain hydraulic fluid. SUBTASK 29-18-21-160-001 (3) If it is necessary, clean all hydraulic fluid from the installation area. (a) Do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803. SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-001 (4) Install the plugs on the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [10], and hydraulic line [15] and caps on the ports of the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. SUBTASK 29-18-21-020-002 (5) Remove the reservoir fill selector valve [6]: (a) Remove the nuts [9], washers [8], washers [5], bolts [4], and spacers [7] from the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. (b) Remove the reservoir fill selector valve [6] from the airplane. 29-18-21 (c) If the new reservoir fill selector valve [6] does not have union [11], union [14], and check valve [2] installed, do these steps: 1) Remove the union [11], union [14], and check valve [2]. 2) Remove and discard the packing [3], packing [12], and packing [13].

E. Reservoir Fill Selector Valve Installation

SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-002 (1) If the check valve, unions, and packings are not installed on the new reservoir fill selector valve [6], do these steps: (a) Lubricate the new packing [3], new packing [13], new packing [12], union [14], and union [11] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Remove the caps from the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. (c) Install the check valve [2] and packing [3] on the port of the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. (d) Install the union [14] and packing [13] on the port of the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. (e) Install the union [11] and packing [12] on the port of the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-003 (2) Install the reservoir fill selector valve [6]: (a) Put the reservoir fill selector valve [6] in its position. 29-18-21 (b) Install the spacers [7], bolts [4], washers [5], washers [8], and nuts [9] that attach the reservoir fill selector valve [6] to the airplane structure. SUBTASK 29-18-21-080-001 (3) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [10], and hydraulic line [15]. SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-004 (4) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [10], and hydraulic line [15] to the reservoir fill selector valve [6]. SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-007 (5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [1] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m). SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-005 (6) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [15] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). F. Reservoir Fill Selector Valve Installation Test SUBTASK 29-18-21-610-001 (1) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 29-18-21-790-001 (2) Make sure that there is no hydraulic leakage at the reservoir fill selector valve [6].

(b) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5-3 flight controls panel, to the STBY RUD position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. (c) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ARM position.

ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. 1) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP NOTE: This CB was opened during the previous step to put the airplane in the Air Mode. 2) Make sure that the standby EMDP operates. (s) Put the airplane in the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. (t) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the ON position.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-035 (1) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 4 C01392 STICK SHAKER LEFT F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name B 6 C01393 STICK SHAKER RIGHT SUBTASK 29-21-00-410-001 (2) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 29-21-00-020-002 (3) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the nose wheel steering mechanism (TASK 32-00-01-080-801). 29-21-00 SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-010 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) Pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-011 (5) Set the flap control lever to the FLAP UP position. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-012 (6) Remove power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
