Number Name/Location 192BR ECS Ram Air Inlet Mixing Duct Panel - Forward

E. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-024 (1) Pressurize the hydraulic system B reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-014 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU REMOVE HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-015 (3) Set the flap control lever to the one-unit position. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-016 (4) Remove hydraulic power from system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. 29-21-00 SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-017 (5) Set the FLT CONTROL A, B, and ALTERNATE FLAPS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 29-21-00-480-001 (6) Install the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163: (a) Do not operate the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) or Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) with the portable hydraulic cart return and pressure lines connected. NOTE: This may prevent the pumps from receiving enough hydraulic fluid from their respective reservoirs and cavitate the pump. (b) Disconnect the pressure line for the standby EMDP . (c) Connect the pressure line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the pressure line for the standby EMDP . 1) Do not connect the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163,to the flexible line from the standby EMDP . (d) You can connect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163,to the either the system B ground service return port, or the standby system reservoir. 1) Connect the supply line to the airplane at one of these locations: NOTE: The system B reservoir and the standby reservoir are connected by a balance line. a) To connect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the system B ground service return port, do these steps. <1> Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192BR ECS Ram Air Inlet Mixing Duct Panel - Forward <2> Connect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the system B ground service return port located forward of the right wheel well. b) To connect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the standby system reservoir, do these steps. <1> Disconnect the supply line for the standby system EMDP at the quick disconnect fitting below the standby reservoir. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . <2> Connect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the quick disconnect fitting on the bottom of the standby reservoir. 29-21-00 SUBTASK 29-21-00-020-001 (7) Disconnect the electrical connector from the standby EMDP . F. System Test of the Standby Hydraulic System SUBTASK 29-21-00-730-001 (1) Do a pressure test of the standby hydraulic system: (a) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ARM position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (b) Slowly increase the pressure from the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to 3000 psig (211 kg/cm 2). 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light goes off when the pressure is between 1100 psig (77 kg/cm 2) and 1500 psig (105 kg/cm 2). (c) Slowly decrease the pressure from the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light comes on when the pressure is between 1500 psig (105 kg/cm 2) and 1000 psig (70 kg/cm 2). (d) Release all the pressure from the standby hydraulic system. 1) If it is necessary, operate the rudder to remove pressure from the standby hydraulic system. (e) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 29-21-00-080-001 (2) Remove the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, from the airplane: (a) Disconnect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, from the airplane. 1) If the supply line is connected to the system B ground service return port, do these steps. a) Disconnect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, from the system B ground service return port located forward of the right wheel well. b) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192BR ECS Ram Air Inlet Mixing Duct Panel - Forward 2) If the supply line is connected to the standby system reservoir, do these steps. a) Disconnect the supply line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, from the quick disconnect fitting on the bottom of standby system reservoir. 29-21-00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . b) Connect the supply line for the standby EMDP to the quick disconnect fitting on the bottom of the standby reservoir. (b) Disconnect the pressure line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, from the pressure line for the standby EMDP . SUBTASK 29-21-00-480-002 (3) Connect the standby test adapter, SPL-8419, to the pressure line from the standby EMDP . (a) Connect the pressure line from the standby EMDP to the pressure port on the standby EMDP . SUBTASK 29-21-00-420-001 (4) Connect the electrical connector to the standby EMDP . SUBTASK 29-21-00-730-002 (5) Do a system test of the standby hydraulic system: WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the STDBY RUD position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. 2) Make sure that the pressure becomes stable at 3000 ±200 psig (211 ±14 kg/cm 2). 3) Make sure that the flight control low pressure light system A is off and that the flight control low pressure light system B is on. (b) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. 2) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. (c) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the STDBY RUD position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. 2) Make sure that the standby EMDP operates. 29-21-00 (d) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. 2) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. (e) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ARM position. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP operates. (f) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch to the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. (g) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the ON position. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP does not operate. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS BEFORE YOU PUSH THE AIR SENSING SWITCH. RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (h) Put the airplane in the air mode, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP operates. 2) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. (i) Put the airplane in the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. 2) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. (j) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the OFF position. (k) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the ON position. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP does not operate. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS BEFORE YOU PUSH THE AIR SENSING SWITCH. RUDDER, THRUST REVERSERS, AND LEADING EDGE SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (l) Put the airplane in the air mode, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP operates. 2) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. (m) Put the airplane in the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. 29-21-00 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. 2) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. (n) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the OFF position. (o) Release the pressure from the standby hydraulic system. 1) If it is necessary, operate the rudder to remove pressure from the standby hydraulic system.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 29-21-00-080-002 (1) Remove the standby test adapter, SPL-8419, from the pressure line. (a) Connect the pressure line from the standby EMDP to the pressure line on the standby EMDP after you remove the standby test adapter, SPL-8419. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-022 (2) Put the airplane systems back to their normal on-ground condition, do this task: (TASK 32-09-00-840-802). SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-019 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-020 (4) Set the flap control lever to the UP position. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-021 (5) Remove hydraulic power from system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

29-21-00-700-803Operational Test of the Standby Hydraulic Actuation System ATA 29 · Task 700-803

Task Description

4. Operational Test of the Standby Hydraulic Actuation System NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This test makes sure that the standby hydraulic pump and the related indications operate correctly. This test checks the standby hydraulic pumps low pressure indications through the system A and system B flight control switches, alternate flaps switch and the auto standby system relay.

B. References

E. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door F. Prepare for the Test SUBTASK 29-21-00-480-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201). SUBTASK 29-21-00-420-003 (2) Install the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, in the nose wheel steering mechanism (TASK 32-00-01-480-801). NOTE: The Nose Landing Gear (NLG) will move when the rudder pedals are moved. To prevent the NLG movement, install a lockout pin in the nose wheel steering mechanism. 29-21-00 SUBTASK 29-21-00-040-001 (3) Make sure that the weather radar will not operate. (a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-025 (4) Make sure electrical power is available: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 29-21-00-010-003 (5) To get access to the P92 panel, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-026 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (6) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP NOTE: The standby hydraulic pump circuit breaker is located behind the P92 front panel. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-036 (7) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 4 C01392 STICK SHAKER LEFT F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name B 6 C01393 STICK SHAKER RIGHT NOTE: Opening the stick shaker circuit breakers will prevent unwanted movement of the control column before the airplane is set to air mode. 29-21-00 SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-027 (8) Pressurize the hydraulic system B reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-028 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (9) Pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-029 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (10) Set the flap control lever to the one-unit position. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-030 (11) Remove pressure from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-21-00-860-041 (12) Set the FLT CONTROL A and FLT CONTROL B switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position.

G. Operational Test of the Standby Hydraulic System

SUBTASK 29-21-00-710-002 (1) Do the operational test of the standby hydraulic system with the FLT CONTROL A switch: (a) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the STBY RUD position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, comes on. 2) Make sure that the FLIGHT CONTROL LOW PRESSURE light A is off. 3) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. (b) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, goes off. 2) Make sure that the FLIGHT CONTROL LOW PRESSURE light A is on. 3) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. 29-21-00 (c) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ARM position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light comes on. 2) If it is necessary, operate the rudder to remove the pressure from the standby hydraulic system. (d) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, goes off. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (e) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP NOTE: The standby hydraulic pump circuit breaker is located behind the P92 front panel. (f) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the STBY RUD position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. 2) Make sure that the standby Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) operates. 3) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, goes off. NOTE: The STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light goes off when the system is pressurized. The light can come on momentarily when the pump starts and the system is not at its usual pressure. 4) Move the rudder pedals. 29-21-00 a) Move the rudder pedals to the left forward stop and to the right forward stop at a high rate for 5 cycles and visually check that the rudder surface moves approximately 27 in. (69 cm) left and right from the neutral position. NOTE: The visual check can be done from the ground without physical measurement of the rudder travel. b) Put in full left pedal and slowly release. c) Make sure that the rudder pedals are centered. d) Put in full right pedal and slowly release. e) Make sure that the rudder pedals are centered. f) Do a visual check of the rudder control surface to make sure it is in the approximate neutral position, within the deadband range of the Standby Rudder Control Unit (SRCU). NOTE: The purpose of the visual check is to examine for a large rudder offset from the neutral position that may result from a failure in the input linkage to the SRCU. The visual check can be done from the ground without physical measurement of the position of the rudder surface. (g) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. 2) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops. (h) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ARM position. 1) Make sure that the standby EMDP operates. 2) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, goes off. NOTE: The STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light goes off when the system is pressurized. The light can come on momentarily when the pump starts and the system is not at its usual pressure. E. Standby Hydraulic EMDP Removal

SUBTASK 29-21-21-020-002 (1) Remove the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (a) Remove and discard the lockwire from the electrical connector [12]. (b) Disconnect the electrical connector [12] from the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (c) Put a container below the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] to catch hydraulic fluid. (d) Disconnect the supply line [11], pressure line [10], and case drain line [6] from the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (e) Install caps and plugs on the hydraulic lines and ports. (f) Remove the bolts [2], bolt [14], washers [1], and washer [15] that attach the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] to the airplane structure. (g) Remove the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] from the airplane. SUBTASK 29-21-21-020-004 (2) If it necessary, remove the reducer [4], reducer [5], and reducer [9]. (a) Remove and discard the packing [3], packing [7], packing [8], and cap ports. 29-21-21 SUBTASK 29-21-21-020-005 (3) Remove the drain plug [18]. (a) If the drain plug [18] P/N AN814-2 was installed, discard it. (b) If the drain plug [18] P/N 65-13139-2 was installed, keep it.

G. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 29-21-21-960-001 (1) If the hydraulic pump is removed because of a mechanical malfunction of the pump, do these steps: NOTE: If the airplane experiences repeated failures of a pump at one location, there could be debris in the case drain line, case drain hose, or case drain hose quick-disconnect that cannot be flushed by the accomplishment of this task. Careful examination/cleaning/replacement of the case drain hose or case drain hose quick-disconnect could be required. (a) Examine the case drain line, case drain hose, or case drain hose quick-disconnect for debris or blockage. (b) If debris or blockage is found, clean or replace the case drain hose or quick-disconnect, as applicable. (c) Inspect the standby case drain filter for metal particle contamination (TASK 29-21-41-000-801 and TASK 29-21-41-400-801). SUBTASK 29-21-21-640-001 (2) If the packings, reducers, and drain plug are not installed on the standby hydraulic EMDP [13], do these steps: (a) Lubricate the packings and reducers with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Install the new packing [3], reducer [4], new packing [7], reducer [5], new packing [8], reducer [9], packing [17], and drain plug [18] on the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (c) Tighten the reducer [4] to 110 ±6 in-lb (12.4 ±0.7 N·m). (d) Tighten the reducer [5] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m). (e) Tighten the reducer [9] to 360 ±18 in-lb (40.7 ±2.0 N·m). (f) If the drain plug [18] P/N AN814-2 was installed, replace it with the drain plug [18] P/N 65-13139-2. 1) Tighten the drain plug [18] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m). SUBTASK 29-21-21-100-001 (3) Clean the bolts [2], bolt [14], washers [1], and contact surfaces (TASK 20-10-34-120-801). SUBTASK 29-21-21-100-002 (4) Clean the mating surfaces of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13], jumper [16], and washer [15]. 29-21-21 (a) Clean the mating surface of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] with 60 grit or finer wet/dry aluminum oxide sandpaper, G51464. 1) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist with solvent, B00184, to clean the mating surface of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. 2) If it is necessary, use cotton wiper, G00034, to remove remaining solvent. (b) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist with solvent, B00184, to clean the mating surfaces of the jumper [16] and washer [15]. SUBTASK 29-21-21-860-004 (5) Fill the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] half full with hydraulic fluid through the supply port. SUBTASK 29-21-21-110-001 (6) Apply primer, C00259, to all areas of the fastener holes where bolts [2] will be installed (TASK 51-21-72-370-804). (a) Let primer, C00259, dry.

H. Standby Hydraulic EMDP Installation

SUBTASK 29-21-21-420-001 (1) Install the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (a) Apply sealant, A50110, or sealant, A50155, or sealant, A50296, or sealant, A50231, to the shank, threads, and under the head of the bolt [14]. (b) Apply sealant, A50110, or sealant, A50155, or sealant, A50296, or sealant, A50231, to the mating surfaces of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13], washer [15], and jumper [16]. WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR- BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (c) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, to the shank and threads of the bolts [2]. (d) Put the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] in its position. (e) Install the washers [1], bolts [2], washer [15], bolt [14], and jumper [16] that attach the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] to the airplane structure. (f) Make sure that the squeeze-out of sealant is continuous and visible. (g) Remove the plugs from the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (h) Remove the caps from the supply line [11], pressure line [10], and case drain line [6]. (i) Connect the supply line [11], pressure line [10], and case drain line [6] to the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (j) Tighten the supply line [11] to 450 ±23 in-lb (50.8 ±2.6 N·m). (k) Tighten the pressure line [10] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m). (l) Tighten the case drain line [6] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). (m) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic system EMDP [13] from the standby hydraulic reservoir at the quick-disconnect. NOTE: The quick-disconnect is at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir. (n) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). 29-21-21 1) Use an non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0010 ohm (1.0 milliohm) or less. WARNING DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (o) Manually apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C50104, to the bare metal surfaces of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] (TASK 51-21-41-370-802). (p) Remove the cap from the electrical connector [12]. (q) Connect the electrical connector [12] to the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (r) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225, on the electrical connector [12] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 29-21-21-170-001 (2) If the pump is replaced because of a mechanical malfunction, flush the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Flushing, TASK 29-11-00-170-801.

I. Standby Hydraulic System Electric Motor - Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation Test

SUBTASK 29-21-21-610-001 (1) If it is necessary, fill the standby hydraulic reservoir and hydraulic system B reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 29-21-21-860-005 (2) Pressurize the standby system reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-21-21-860-007 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. 29-21-21 (WARNING PRECEDES) WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (3) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP NOTE: The standby hydraulic pump circuit breaker is located behind the P92 front panel. SUBTASK 29-21-21-860-008 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS AND THE THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) Pressurize the standby hydraulic system to bleed the air out of standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. (a) Set the FLT CONTROL A or FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the STBY RUD position. (b) Make sure that the standby EMDP [13] operates. (c) Make sure that the LOW PRESSURE light is not on. (d) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is on. (e) Operate the rudder slowly through a minimum of two full cycles. (f) Set the FLT CONTROL A or FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position. (g) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, is off. (h) Make sure that there is no hydraulic leakage at the standby hydraulic EMDP [13]. SUBTASK 29-21-21-860-009 (5) Remove the power from the standby hydraulic system, do this task: Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802. SUBTASK 29-21-21-410-001 (6) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 194DR Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel 29-21-21 SUBTASK 29-21-21-410-003 (7) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-001 (1) Release pressure from the system B hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-21-31-020-014 (2) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. 29-21-31 SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-007 (3) Put the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch to the OFF position. SUBTASK 29-21-31-420-014 (4) Attach the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the ALTERNATE FLAPS switch. SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-002 (5) Put the FLT CONTROL A and B switches, on the P5 overhead panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 29-21-31-420-001 (6) Attach the DO NOT OPERATE tags, STD-858, on the FLT CONTROL switches. SUBTASK 29-21-31-020-001 (7) Drain the hydraulic fluid for the standby hydraulic system as follows: (a) Do the steps of either Method 1 or Method 2 to drain the hydraulic fluid from the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]: 1) Do these steps to accomplish Method 1: CAUTION PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . a) Disconnect the supply line [21] for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect [15] at the bottom of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. b) Connect a drain hose, SPL-6107, to the quick-disconnect [15] on the bottom of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. c) Put the end of the drain hose, SPL-6107, into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. d) Drain the hydraulic fluid into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. NOTE: System B reservoir will drain also. NOTE: The standby hydraulic reservoir contains approximately 3.5 gal (13.2 l). e) Disconnect the drain hose, SPL-6107, from the quick-disconnect [15] on the bottom of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . f) Reconnect the supply line [21] at the quick-disconnect [15] on the bottom of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. 2) Do these steps to accomplish Method 2: 29-21-31 a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 194DR Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel b) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, below the standby Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP). c) Disconnect the supply line [21] at the standby EMDP . d) Put the disconnected end of the supply line [21] into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. e) Allow the hydraulic fluid from the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1] to drain into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. f) Reconnect the supply line [21] to the standby EMDP . g) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 194DR Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel 3) Drain the hydraulic fluid collected from the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1] into a 50 Gallon (190 l) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-3901. SUBTASK 29-21-31-160-001 (8) If you get hydraulic fluid on the airplane, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803. SUBTASK 29-21-31-020-010 (10) Remove the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. (a) Discard the packing [3] and packings [8]. SUBTASK 29-21-31-020-013 (13) Install caps on the ports in the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1] to prevent contamination.

AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . (8) Connect the supply line [21] to the standby reservoir quick-disconnect [15] at the bottom of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. SUBTASK 29-21-31-420-009 (9) Remove the cap from the electrical connector for the low quantity switch [2]. SUBTASK 29-21-31-420-010 (10) Connect the electrical connector to the low quantity switch [2]. SUBTASK 29-21-31-420-011 (11) Do these steps to install the bonding jumper [9]: (a) Abrasive clean the mating surface of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1] and solvent clean the terminal of the bonding jumper [9], washer [10], and nut [11] (SWPM 20-20-00). (b) Install the bonding jumper [9], washer [10], and nut [11] on the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1]. (c) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1] and adjacent structure (SWPM 20-20-10). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0005 ohms (0.5 milliohms) or less. (d) Apply sealant, A02315, to the jumper terminal connection (SWPM 20-20-10).

G. Standby System Reservoir Installation Test

SUBTASK 29-21-31-210-002 (1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW QUANTITY , on the P5 overhead panel, FLT CONT and left and right MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P2 panel, are on. 29-21-31 SUBTASK 29-21-31-610-001 (2) Do the servicing for the standby and system B hydraulic reservoirs: (a) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-29-1106 SUBTASK 29-21-31-080-001 (3) Remove the lockset, SPL-1795. SUBTASK 29-21-31-420-012 (4) Close the system B hydraulic reservoir depressurization valve. RYR ALL SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-003 (5) Pressurize the standby and system B hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-21-31-930-001 (6) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tags from the FLT CONTROL switches. SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE RUDDER AND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE RUDDER AND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (7) Put the FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 overhead panel, to the STDBY RUD position. (a) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STDBY RUD ON light, on the P5 overhead panel, is on. SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-005 (8) Operate the rudder full travel in each direction for a minimum of three times. (a) Make sure that the STDBY HYD LOW QUANTITY light stays off. SUBTASK 29-21-31-860-006 (9) Put the FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 overhead panel, to the OFF position. (a) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 overhead panel, is off. SUBTASK 29-21-31-790-001 (10) Do a check of the standby hydraulic system reservoir [1] and all connections for leaks.

D. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-001 (1) Pressurize the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-058 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE HEAT OF THE SENSOR IS NOT ON. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (2) Make sure that the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensor heat is off. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-003 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE SENSOR FOR THE ANGLE OF ATTACK (AOA) IS COOL BEFORE YOU TOUCH IT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (3) Make sure that the two AOA sensor vanes are at the zero position. NOTE: You can use your hands to move the AOA sensor vanes. (a) Use the angle of attack probe test fixture, SPL-1917. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-004 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM ALL CONTROL SURFACES AND THE NOSE GEAR WHEN HYDRAULIC POWER IS SUPPLIED. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, AND THE NOSE GEAR ARE SUPPLIED WITH POWER BY THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS. INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR WHEN HYDRAULIC POWER IS SUPPLIED. (4) Supply hydraulic power to systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-005 WARNING KEEP ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES AND THE FLIGHT CONTROL DRIVE MECHANISMS. THESE COMPONENTS WILL MOVE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Move the flap control lever to the 5 unit position. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-006 (6) Once the flaps stop moving, remove the hydraulic power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. 29-22-00

E. PTU Operational Test

SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-007 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Put the ALTERNATE FLAPS arm switch, on the P5 panel, to the ARM position. (a) Make sure that the standby hydraulic pump operates. SUBTASK 29-22-00-710-001 (2) Momentarily move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch, on the P5 panel, to the DOWN position and immediately move it back to the OFF position. (a) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the fully extended position. NOTE: The Leading Edge (LE) FLAPS TRANSIT light will stay on. NOTE: The LE devices can retract a small amount when you move them to the fully extended position. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-008 (3) Put the ALTERNATE FLAPS arm switch to the OFF position. (a) Make sure that the standby hydraulic pump stops. SUBTASK 29-22-00-210-001 CAUTION PRESSURIZE THE RESERVOIR TO THE CORRECT PRESSURE. THE INCORRECT PRESSURE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE CHECK VALVE FOR THE PTU. (4) Check the pressure for the system B hydraulic reservoir. NOTE: Pressure gages for the system B hydraulic reservoir are above the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) in the main wheel well. (a) Make sure that the system B hydraulic reservoir has a pressure of 45 psig (310 kPa) - 65 psig (448 kPa). SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-009 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL CHOCKS AT THE WHEELS. THE BRAKES WILL RELEASE WHEN YOU PUT THE AIRPLANE IN AIR MODE. THIS CAN CAUSE THE AIRPLANE TO MOVE SUDDENLY . IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL THE CHOCKS, INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (5) Make sure that the wheels have chocks around them (TASK 10-11-05-500-801, TASK 10-11-05-500-802). 29-22-00 SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-056 WARNING DO NOT LIFT THE AIRPLANE ON JACKS, IF YOU USE THE ENGINE-DRIVEN PUMP (EDP) TO PRESSURIZE THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. THE AIRPLANE CAN MOVE SUDDENLY IF THE ENGINE OPERATES WITH THE AIRPLANE ON JACKS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (6) Put the airplane to the air mode, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. NOTE: When the airplane is put in the air mode with the engines running, the engines will advance to flight idle speed. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-050 (7) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 15 C01081 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 1 A 16 C01085 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 2 SUBTASK 29-22-00-210-002 (8) Make sure that the Power Transfer Unit (PTU) starts. SUBTASK 29-22-00-210-003 (9) Make sure that the leading edge slats retract to the intermediate position. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-010 (10) Put the airplane to the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 29-22-00-710-002 (11) Check the PTU check valve, do the steps that follow: (a) Remove pressure from the hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. (b) Put the airplane to the air mode, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. (c) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 15 C01081 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 1 A 16 C01085 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 2 (d) Supply hydraulic power to system B with the EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803. (e) Move the flap control lever to the 1 unit position. (f) Make sure that the PTU control valve is open. (g) Feel and listen to the PTU to make sure that it does not operate. (h) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure in system A does not increase. (i) If the PTU operates or the pressure in hydraulic system A increases, do these steps: 1) Replace the PTU check valve. 29-22-00 2) Replace the PTU, do these tasks: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal, TASK 29-22-11-000-801, Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation, TASK 29-22-11-400-801. 3) Replace the PTU pressure filter element, do these tasks: PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801, PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation, TASK 29-22-21-400-802. (j) Put the airplane to the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-019 (1) Move the flap control lever, on the control stand, to the UP position. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-020 (2) Remove the hydraulic power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-021 (3) Return the airplane to its usual on ground condition, do this task: Return the Airplane Systems Back to Their Normal On Ground Condition, TASK 32-09-00-840-802.

BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (9) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-025 (10) If the flaps are not fully retracted, retract them: WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. (a) Pressurize hydraulic power to the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (14) Pressurize the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. 29-22-00 SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-033 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. NOTE: The electric motor driven pump does not have the capacity to operate the PTU correctly. (a) Make sure that the PTU does not operate. (22) Turn the left AOA vane counterclockwise until the leading edge slats extend. (a) Make sure that the leading edge slats extend fully, equally, and smoothly. (b) Use a stopwatch, STD-1139, to make sure that the time necessary to extend the leading edge slats is not more than 4 seconds. SUBTASK 29-22-00-730-007 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT STAY AWAY FROM THE LEADING EDGE SLATS, TRAILING EDGE FLAPS, AND DRIVE MECHANISMS. SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-001 (7) Open the drain valve on the system B reservoir. 29-22-11 (a) Remove and discard the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the reservoir drain valve. SUBTASK 29-22-11-010-001 (8) Fully drain the system B reservoir in a 50 Gallon (190 l) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-3901. SUBTASK 29-22-11-010-003 (9) Open the drain valve on the system A reservoir. (a) Remove and discard the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the reservoir drain valve. (a) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the applicable reservoir drain valve with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or TASK 20-10-44-400-802).

G. PTU Removal

SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-002 (1) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] from the power transfer unit [10]. (a) Put a container below the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] to catch the hydraulic fluid. (b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] from the power transfer unit [10]. (c) Install caps on the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21]. SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-003 (2) Remove the power transfer unit [10]. (a) Remove the bolts [11] and washers [12] that attach the power transfer unit [10] to the airplane structure. (b) Remove the power transfer unit [10]. SUBTASK 29-22-11-020-002 (3) Remove the check valve [24] from the union [2]. SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-004 (4) Remove the union [2], union [5], union [8], union [13], union [16], union [20], and port-drain [22]. (a) Discard the packing [3], packing [4], packing [9], packing [14], packing [18], packing [19], and packing [23]. (b) Install the plugs in the hydraulic ports of the power transfer unit [10].

Prepare for the Installation SUBTASK 29-22-11-200-001 (1) If the power transfer unit [10] is replaced because of mechanical malfunction, do these steps: (a) Replace the power transfer unit [10] pressure filter, do these tasks: 1) PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801. 2) PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation, TASK 29-22-21-400-802. 29-22-11 (b) Replace the A system return filter, do these tasks: 1) Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801. 2) Return Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-61-400-801. (c) Replace the B system return filter, do these tasks: 1) Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801. 2) Return Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-61-400-801.

G. PTU Installation

SUBTASK 29-22-11-640-001 (1) Install the hydraulic fittings in the power transfer unit [10]. (a) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic ports in the power transfer unit [10]. (b) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the new packing [3], new packing [4], new packing [9], new packing [14], new packing [18], new packing [19], and new packing [23]. (c) Install the packing [3], packing [4], packing [9], packing [14], packing [18], packing [19], and packing [23], with the union [2], union [5], union [8], union [13], union [16], union [20], and port-drain [22] in the power transfer unit [10]. 1) Tighten the union [2] and union [20] to 99 in-lb (11.2 N·m) - 121 in-lb (13.7 N·m). 2) Tighten the union [8] to 153 in-lb (17.3 N·m) - 187 in-lb (21.1 N·m). 3) Tighten the union [13] and union [16] to 252 in-lb (28.5 N·m) - 308 in-lb (34.8 N·m). 4) Tighten the union [5] to 324 in-lb (36.6 N·m) - 396 in-lb (44.7 N·m). 5) Tighten the port-drain [22] to 99 in-lb (11.2 N·m) - 121 in-lb (13.7 N·m). SUBTASK 29-22-11-420-003 (2) Install the check valve [24] on the union [2]. SUBTASK 29-22-11-100-001 (3) Fill the power transfer unit [10] (motor and pump) with hydraulic fluid, D00153, until it is approximately one-half full. SUBTASK 29-22-11-420-001 CAUTION INSTALL THE POWER TRANSFER UNIT (PTU) WITH THE MOTOR ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE AIRPLANE. IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL THE PTU CORRECTLY , THE SYSTEM WILL NOT OPERATE. (4) Install the power transfer unit [10]. (a) Put the power transfer unit [10] in its position in the airplane with the motor on the left side. (b) Install the bolts [11] and washers [12] to attach the power transfer unit [10] to the airplane structure. (c) Remove the protective caps from the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21]. (d) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] to the power transfer unit [10]. 1) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [1] and hydraulic line [21] to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 284 in-lb (32.1 N·m). 29-22-11 2) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [7] and hydraulic line [15] to 475 in-lb (53.7 N·m) - 525 in-lb (59.3 N·m). 3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [6] to 427 in-lb (48.2 N·m) - 473 in-lb (53.4 N·m). 4) Tighten the B-nut on the T-fitting [17] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m). SUBTASK 29-22-11-610-002 (5) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

(b) Remove the plugs from the inlet and outlet ports of the filter assembly [7]. (c) Install the packings [2] and reducers [3] in the inlet and outlet ports of the filter assembly [7]. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-004 (2) Put the filter assembly [7] in its position with the flow direction arrow outboard and filter bowl [11] down. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-005 (3) Install the bolts [10], washers [9], washers [6], and nuts [5] to attach the filter assembly [7] to the airplane structure. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-006 (4) Remove the caps from the hydraulic lines [4]. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-007 (5) Connect the hydraulic lines [4] to the filter assembly [7]. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-016 (6) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [4] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m). SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-018 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-009 (4) Install the packing [14] and backup ring [13] in the filter element [12]. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-010 (5) Install the filter element [12] in the filter bowl [11]. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-017 (7) Put the filter bowl [11] and filter element [12] under the filter assembly [7]. (a) Raise the filter element [12] from the filter bowl [11] and push it onto the filter assembly [7] outlet. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-011 (8) Install the filter bowl [11] on the filter head [1]. SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-012 (9) Torque the filter bowl [11] to 300 ±60 in-lb (34 ±7 N·m). 29-22-21 SUBTASK 29-22-21-420-015 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . (10) Reconnect the system B EMDP self-seal quick-disconnect [17]. (4) Pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 29-22-21-860-011 (5) Move the flap control lever to the UP position to fully retract the flaps and slats. SUBTASK 29-22-21-860-012 (6) Move the flap control lever to the 5 unit position to extend the leading edge slats to the EXTEND position. SUBTASK 29-22-21-860-013 (7) Remove power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-22-21-860-014 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PTU CHECK VALVE IF YOU OPERATE THE PTU WITHOUT PRESSURE IN THE HYDRAULIC RESERVOIR. (9) Look at the pressure gages for the system B hydraulic reservoir. NOTE: The pressure gages is above the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP). The EMDP is installed in the main wheel well. (a) Make sure that the system B reservoir has a pressure of 45 psig (310 kPa) - 65 psig (448 kPa). SUBTASK 29-22-21-710-003 WARNING MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LEADING EDGE SLATS DURING THIS PROCEDURE. THE SLATS CAN MOVE AUTOMATICALLY (UNLESS OTHERWISE INHIBITED) WHEN THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM IS PRESSURIZED, THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS ARE EXTENDED AND THE AIR TO GROUND RELAYS SENSE AN AIRBORNE CONDITION. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (10) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name C 15 C01355 LANDING GEAR AIR/GND SYS 2 SUBTASK 29-22-21-210-003 (11) Make sure that the Power Transfer Unit (PTU) starts. NOTE: Listen to and feel the PTU to make sure that it starts. SUBTASK 29-22-21-710-004 (12) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name C 15 C01355 LANDING GEAR AIR/GND SYS 2 SUBTASK 29-22-21-210-004 (13) Make sure that the PTU stops. NOTE: Listen to and feel the PTU to make sure that it stops. SUBTASK 29-22-21-790-001 (14) Examine the filter module and connections for leaks. SUBTASK 29-22-21-860-015 (15) Remove power from hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-22-21-610-001 (16) If it is necessary, fill the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. 29-22-21

SUBTASK 29-22-31-020-007 (9) Install caps on the electrical connector [2], hydraulic lines, and open ports on the control valve [1] to prevent contamination or damage.

To depressurize, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-22-41-020-001 (1) Disconnect the electrical connector [2] from the pressure switch [1]. SUBTASK 29-22-41-020-006 (2) Remove the lockwire. 29-22-41 SUBTASK 29-22-41-020-002 (3) Remove the pressure switch [1]. SUBTASK 29-22-41-020-003 (4) Remove the packing [3] from the pressure switch [1]. SUBTASK 29-22-41-020-004 (5) Install protective caps on the electrical connector [2] and the open port on the pressure module to prevent contamination or damage.

G. EDP Pressure Switch Auto Slat System Installation

SUBTASK 29-22-41-640-001 (1) Lubricate the new packing [3] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 29-22-41-420-001 (2) Do these steps to install the pressure switch [1] in the hydraulic system B pressure module: (a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol, B50262, or alcohol, B00068, to clean the mating surfaces of the pressure switch [1] and pressure module. (b) Install the packing [3] on the pressure switch [1]. (c) Remove the plug from the pressure module. (d) Put the pressure switch [1] in the pressure module. (e) Tighten the pressure switch [1] to 161 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 179 in-lb (20.2 N·m). (f) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the pressure switch [1] and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. 29-22-41 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0005 ohm (0.50 milliohm) or less. (g) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912. SUBTASK 29-22-41-420-002 (3) Remove the cap from the electrical connector [2]. SUBTASK 29-22-41-210-006 (4) Before you connect the electrical connector [2], examine the electrical connector [2] for corrosion. WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES AT AIRPORTS THAT USE DEICING FLUID WHICH CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE. ALSO DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR IS PART OF A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT . (a) If there was corrosion, refer to SWPM 20-60-03 to correct the problem. (b) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171 to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). SUBTASK 29-22-41-420-003 (5) Connect the electrical connector [2] to the pressure switch [1]. SUBTASK 29-22-41-440-001 (6) Put the FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 panel, to the ON position.

(1) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00768 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS B 29-22-51 Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name C 8 C00767 ELEC HYD PUMP CONTROL SYS A F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP SUBTASK 29-22-51-410-001 (2) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 29-22-51-860-010 (3) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 15 C01081 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 1 A 16 C01085 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 2 SUBTASK 29-22-51-710-001 (4) Do this task: Power Transfer Unit Operational Test, TASK 29-22-00-710-801. 29-32-00-730-802Case Drain Overheat Switch Test (Preferred Method) ATA 29 · Task 730-802

Task Description

2. Case Drain Overheat Switch Test (Preferred Method) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This test will functionally check the hydraulic system A & B case drain overheat switches and the associated OVERHEAT lights (ELEC 1 & 2) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5). (2) With increasing temperature, the overheat switch contacts close at 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C). With decreasing temperature, overheat switch contacts open at minimum 165°F (73.9°C). The OVERHEAT lights (ELEC 1 & 2) come on when the overheat switches are closed.

B. References

Reference Title 29-32-12-000-801 Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Removal (P/B 401) 29-32-12-400-801 Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-3924 Tester - Thermo Switch, K-Type Thermocouple Switches Part #: H394R Supplier: 98869 Opt Part #: H294 Supplier: 98869 Opt Part #: H394 SERIES Supplier: 98869 SPL-3952 Kit - Heater Probes, TEMPCAL Part #: BH24944-13 Supplier: 98869 Part #: BH24944-14 Supplier: 98869 Part #: BH24944-16 Supplier: 98869 29-32-00

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

E. Case Drain Overheat Switch Test (Hydraulic System A)

SUBTASK 29-32-00-020-002 (1) Remove the system A case drain overheat switch (S798). To remove it, do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Removal, TASK 29-32-12-000-801. (a) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 (b) Reconnect electrical connector D2688 to the overheat switch (S798). (c) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 SUBTASK 29-32-00-480-001 (2) Connect the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and heater probe BH16440-40 to the overheat switch. NOTE: The heater probe BH16440-40 is for use with the hydraulic fluid overheat warning switches, and is found in the following heater probe kit(s): TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-3952. SUBTASK 29-32-00-720-001 (3) Do these steps to functionally check the overheat switch: NOTE: The following steps should be repeated twice. (a) Do a check of the overheat switch's actuation "closed" temperature: 1) Stabilize the overheat switch temperature at 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C) for a minimum of two (2) minutes. 2) Slowly increase the overheat switch temperature at a rate of 5+/-1 degrees F/minute (2.8+/-0.6 degrees C/minute) until the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5) comes on. 3) Make a record of the temperature when OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) came on. 4) Make sure that the overheat switch actuated "closed" at a temperature of 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C) when the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) came on. (b) Do a check of the overheat switch's actuation "open" temperature: 1) Slowly decrease the overheat switch temperature at a rate of 5+/-1 degrees F/minute (2.8+/-0.6 degrees C/minute) until the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5) goes off. 2) Make a record of the temperature when OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) went off. 29-32-00 3) Make sure that the overheat switch actuated "open" at a temperature no less than 165°F (73.9°C) when the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) went off. (c) Make sure that there is no less than 5 degrees F (2.8 degrees C) of temperature differential between the recorded temperatures of the overheat switch "closed" and "open" actuations. (d) Do each of the above steps a second time. SUBTASK 29-32-00-080-001 (4) Disconnect the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and heater probe BH16440-40 from the overheat switch. SUBTASK 29-32-00-420-001 (5) Reinstall the system A case drain overheat switch (S798): (a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 (b) Disconnect electrical connector D2688 from overheat switch (S798). (c) Install the system A case drain overheat switch (S798). To install it, do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation, TASK 29-32-12-400-801. (d) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 F. Case Drain Overheat Switch Test (Hydraulic System B) SUBTASK 29-32-00-020-003 (1) Remove the system B case drain overheat switch (S799). To remove it, do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Removal, TASK 29-32-12-000-801. (a) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5 (b) Reconnect electrical connector D2690 to the overheat switch (S799). (c) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5 SUBTASK 29-32-00-480-002 (2) Connect the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and heater probe BH16440-40 to the overheat switch. NOTE: The heater probe BH16440-40 is for use with the hydraulic fluid overheat warning switches, and is found in the following heater probe kit(s): TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-3952. 29-32-00 SUBTASK 29-32-00-720-002 (3) Do these steps to functionally check the overheat switch: NOTE: The following steps should be repeated twice. (a) Do a check of the overheat switch's actuation "closed" temperature: 1) Stabilize the overheat switch temperature at 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C) for a minimum of two (2) minutes. 2) Slowly increase the overheat switch temperature at a rate of 5+/-1 degrees F/minute (2.8+/-0.6 degrees C/minute) until the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 1) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5) comes on. 3) Make a record of the temperature when OVERHEAT light (ELEC 1) came on. 4) Make sure that the overheat switch actuated "closed" at a temperature of 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C) when the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 1) came on. (b) Do a check of the overheat switch's actuation "open" temperature: 1) Slowly decrease the overheat switch temperature at a rate of 5+/-1 degrees F/minute (2.8+/-0.6 degrees C/minute) until the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 1) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5) goes off. 2) Make a record of the temperature when OVERHEAT light (ELEC 1) went off. 3) Make sure that the overheat switch actuated "open" at a temperature no less than 165°F (73.9°C) when the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 1) went off. (c) Make sure that there is no less than 5 degrees F (2.8 degrees C) of temperature differential between the recorded temperatures of the overheat switch "closed" and "open" actuations. (d) Do each of the above steps a second time. SUBTASK 29-32-00-080-002 (4) Disconnect the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and heater probe BH16440-40 from the overheat switch. SUBTASK 29-32-00-420-002 (5) Reinstall the system B case drain overheat switch (S799): (a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5 (b) Disconnect electrical connector D2690 from overheat switch (S799). (c) Install the system B case drain overheat switch (S799). To install it, do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation, TASK 29-32-12-400-801. (d) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5

(e) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 (f) On connector D2688 remove the jumper wire from pin A to pin B. 29-32-00 (g) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 (h) Make sure the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5) went off. (e) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5 (f) On connector D2690 remove the jumper wire from pin A to pin B. E. Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation

SUBTASK 29-32-12-080-002 (1) Remove the cover from the port of the switch tee. SUBTASK 29-32-12-640-001 (2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packings [1] and fittings threads. SUBTASK 29-32-12-420-002 (3) Install the packing [1] and overheat switch [2] in the open port of the switch tee. (a) Tighten the overheat switch [2] to 450 ±23 in-lb (50.8 ±2.6 N·m). SUBTASK 29-32-12-080-001 (4) Remove the protective cap from the electrical connector [3]. SUBTASK 29-32-12-420-004 (5) Connect the electrical connector [3] to the overheat switch [2]. SUBTASK 29-32-12-860-003 (6) For hydraulic system A, remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6 SUBTASK 29-32-12-860-009 (7) For hydraulic system B, remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name F 11 C00317 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 5 SUBTASK 29-32-12-420-005 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY TO DO THE INSTALLATION, DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER THE INSTALLATION, MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 INCH. IF THE INDICATOR PINS DO NOT CORRECTLY EXTEND, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR OR THE PUMP . (8) Connect the supply line quick-disconnect. 29-32-12 F. Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation Test SUBTASK 29-32-12-600-001 (1) If it is necessary, fill the hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 29-32-12-860-004 (2) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807. SUBTASK 29-32-12-860-005 (3) For the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803. SUBTASK 29-32-12-790-001 (4) Examine the overheat switch [2] for leaks. SUBTASK 29-32-12-860-006 (5) For the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

D. Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Transmitter/Indicator Removal

SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-002 (1) Remove the power from the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-010 (2) If the hydraulic system B fluid quantity transmitter/indicator is being removed, do this task: Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802. SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-003 (3) Release the pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-002 WARNING DO NOT CLOSE THE DRAIN VALVE UNTIL YOU REPLACE THE TRANSMITTER. IF YOU CLOSE THE DRAIN VALVE, FLUID CAN COLLECT IN THE RESERVOIR. THEN IT CAN GET ON PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT WHEN YOU REMOVE THE TRANSMITTER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) Open the drain valve. (a) Remove and discard the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the drain valve. NOTE: Do not close the drain valve until you replace the transmitter. 29-33-12 SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-004 (5) Drain the applicable system reservoir into a 15 gallon (57 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-6907. SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-005 (6) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name D 5 C01359 DISPLAY DEU 1 PRI F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 11 C01360 DISPLAY DEU 2 PRI SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-003 (7) Disconnect the electrical connector [2]. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-006 (8) Install a protective cap on the electrical connector [2]. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-007 (9) Remove the mounting bolts [3], the washers [4] (under the bolthead), the washers [6] (under the nut), and the nuts [7]. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-005 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE TRANSMITTER-FLOAT DOES NOT TOUCH THE INTERNAL STAND PIPE. IF THE TRANSMITTER-FLOAT TOUCHES THE INTERNAL STAND PIPE, DAMAGE TO THE TRANSMITTER-FLOAT CAN OCCUR. (10) Carefully remove the transmitter [1] from the reservoir through the reservoir opening. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-008 (11) Remove the packing [5]. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-009 (12) Discard the packing [5].

E. Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Transmitter/Indicator Inspection

SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-001 (1) Release pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-001 (2) Open the drain valve on the bottom of the hydraulic reservoir. (a) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the drain valve. SUBTASK 29-33-12-680-001 (3) Drain the fluid into a 15 gallon (57 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-6907. SUBTASK 29-33-12-420-001 (4) Close the drain valve. SUBTASK 29-33-12-420-002 (5) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the reservoir drain valve with double twist method. 29-33-12 SUBTASK 29-33-12-610-001 (6) Slowly fill the applicable hydraulic reservoir with the fluid quantity specified below, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. NOTE: The fluid quantities are correct only if all supply and return lines to the reservoir are full. (a) The fluid quantity must be 5.7 gal (21.6 l) for the system A. (b) The fluid quantity must be 8.2 gal (31.0 l) for the system B. SUBTASK 29-33-12-210-001 (7) Make sure that the fluid level on the transmitter indicator and the cockpit indicator increases as you fill the reservoir. (a) If the fluid level does not increase, refer to the Observed Fault List in the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM). SUBTASK 29-33-12-210-002 (8) Make sure that the indicators on the transmitters show full when the system A reservoir is 5.7 gal (21.6 l) and system B reservoir is 8.2 gal (31.0 l). (a) When the indicators on the reservoir transmitters show full, make sure that the HYD Q % indicators on the Systems display show 100 +6%/-9%. (b) If the transmitters and/or the engine display fail to meet these requirements, refer to the Observed Fault List in the FIM.

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 29-33-21-860-001 (1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name E 14 C00316 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 4 29-33-21 SUBTASK 29-33-21-860-002 (2) Remove the hydraulic power from system B and the standby system. (a) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. (b) Do this task: Standby Hydraulic System Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802. SUBTASK 29-33-21-860-003 (3) Release pressure from the system B hydraulic reservoir. (a) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. RYR 006, 007, 013, 014 PRE SB 737-29-1106 SUBTASK 29-33-21-480-001 (4) Install the lockset, SPL-1795, on the system B depressurization valve when the valve is open. RYR ALL SUBTASK 29-33-21-020-001 (5) Drain the standby hydraulic reservoir, do these steps: CAUTION PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . (a) Disconnect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir. (b) If a spare quick-disconnect hose assembly is available, do the following steps: 1) Put the hose end of the spare quick-disconnect hose assembly into 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. 2) Connect the quick-disconnect end of the spare hose assembly to the standby reservoir. (c) If a spare quick-disconnect hose is not available, do the following steps: 1) Disconnect the supply hose at the standby hydraulic pump (TASK 29-21-21-000-801). 2) Put the end of the standby pump supply hose into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . 3) Connect the quick-disconnect end of the supply hose to the standby reservoir. (d) Drain the hydraulic fluid into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154. NOTE: The standby hydraulic reservoir contains approximately 3.6 gal (13.6 l). 29-33-21 SUBTASK 29-33-21-080-002 (6) If a spare quick-disconnect hose assembly was used to drain the standby hydraulic reservoir, do these steps: (a) Remove the spare quick-disconnect hose assembly. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . (b) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir. SUBTASK 29-33-21-080-003 (7) If the supply hose to the standby hydraulic pump was disconnected to drain the standby reservoir, connect it to the supply port of the pump (TASK 29-21-21-400-801). SUBTASK 29-33-21-420-007 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP . (8) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir. SUBTASK 29-33-21-160-001 (9) If you get hydraulic fluid on the airplane, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.

E. Standby Reservoir Low Quantity Switch Removal

SUBTASK 29-33-21-020-003 (3) Remove the low quantity switch [2] from the standby hydraulic system reservoir [4]. SUBTASK 29-33-21-020-004 (4) Remove the packing [3].
